title: archive_boot deletes live @ then fails to recreate it (name mismatch + delete-before-lookup)
description:
CONFIRMED from source + live config on 2026-08-27, from ultrareview finding merged_bug_004 (PR #42). Independently re-derived; not taken on the reviewer's word.

TWO defects that only bite in combination:

(a) ORDERING — indexer/src/backup.rs archive_boot(): the sequence is snapshot -r (archive) -> btrfs subvolume DELETE live @ -> find_latest_btrbk_snapshot() -> recreate. The lookup happens AFTER the delete, and the None branch only logs a Warning, so a failed lookup leaves the live subvolume deleted. scripts/backup-run.sh update_boot_subvolumes() does the opposite and correct thing: look up first, 'continue' if nothing found, then create @.new -> delete @ -> mv @.new @. Bash is right; Rust is not. This is exactly the bash/Rust divergence PR #42 priority 4 asked reviewers to check.

(b) NAME MISMATCH — find_latest_btrbk_snapshot (backup.rs:784) builds prefix = format!("nvme/{snap_name}.") and archive_boot maps "@" -> "root". Live /etc/btrbk/btrbk.conf line 28 sets snapshot_name = 'root-' (trailing hyphen, emitted by resolve_snapshot_names disambiguation because line 34 also declares 'root-root'). On-disk names are therefore nvme/root-.<TS>, and "nvme/root-.<TS>".starts_with("nvme/root.") is FALSE. The lookup can never succeed for @.

ASYMMETRY the review did not note: @home maps to snap_name 'home', btrbk.conf line 31 is 'snapshot_name home' (no hyphen), so nvme/home.<TS> DOES match prefix nvme/home. — @home is recreated correctly. Only @ is destroyed. Verified with a standalone Rust program using the real strings: @ -> NO MATCH, @home -> MATCH.

REACHABILITY: config.boot.enabled = true and boot.subvolumes = ['@','@home'] in the live /etc/das-backup/config.toml, and source target_subdirs = ['nvme'] so the nvme/ prefix is otherwise right. archive_boot is the RUST path only — reached from btrdasd-helper (D-Bus/GUI backup) and manual CLI full runs. The scheduled 03:00 job runs backup-run.sh, which is correct, so nightly backups are NOT affected.

IMPACT: on a GUI or manual-CLI full run, the primary target's live bootable @ is deleted and never recreated. The read-only @.archive.<TS> survives, so this is recoverable, not data loss — but it silently defeats the disaster-recovery purpose of the boot archive, and the only signal is one Warning line.
design:
Fix both halves; either alone leaves a live trap.

(a) Hoist find_latest_btrbk_snapshot above the archive/delete and skip the target when it returns None, mirroring update_boot_subvolumes()'s look-up-then-continue. Optionally adopt bash's create-@.new -> delete-@ -> mv sequencing so the live subvolume is never absent even momentarily.

(b) Stop hardcoding the name. Read the snapshot_name values from /etc/btrbk/btrbk.conf — the file btrbk itself consumes — rather than re-deriving them. This is the precedent already set by btrdasd forget (0.7.16.0), whose live-series guard reads btrbk.conf 'so the guard cannot disagree with reality the way a second implementation of the naming rules could'. Deriving from config.toml via resolve_snapshot_names would re-create the same two-implementations problem this bug IS.

Also derive the 'nvme/' subdir from Source.target_subdirs instead of hardcoding it.
acceptance_criteria: find_latest_btrbk_snapshot resolves the real on-disk name for @ against a fixture containing nvme/root-.<TS>; a counter-test proves the test goes RED against the current hardcoded prefix. archive_boot leaves live @ intact when no snapshot is found (test asserts the subvolume still exists after a simulated lookup failure). Verified end-to-end on a real target before closing.
close_reason: VERIFIED END-TO-END ON THE PRODUCTION DAS 2026-08-28. 'btrdasd backup boot-archive' logged: Archived /mnt/backup-22tb/@ -> @.archive.20260828T092758, then 'Created /mnt/backup-22tb/@ from nvme/root-.20260828T0300' — the hyphenated name the pre-0.7.20.0 hardcoded prefix 'nvme/root.' could never match, so under the old code this run would have deleted @ and then failed to recreate it. @home built from nvme/home.20260828T0300 (the asymmetry). Both mirror targets skipped. On-disk confirmation independent of the log: @ and @home exist as real subvolumes, both archives present, NO @.new/@home.new staging left behind, source snapshot present. Also proven by two root-gated loopback tests whose failure was observed against the restored delete-before-lookup ordering.

title: Span join has no source scoping — btrdasd list reports files from unrelated subvolumes
description:
get_files_in_snapshot (indexer/src/db.rs:319) resolves a snapshot's contents with a bare snapshot-id range and no source/series predicate:

    JOIN spans s ON s.file_id = f.id
    WHERE s.first_snap <= ?1 AND s.last_snap >= ?1

Snapshot ids are allocated globally as sources are indexed, so every source's snapshots are interleaved in id space. A span recorded as (first_snap=5, last_snap=81) therefore claims its file is present in EVERY snapshot whose id falls in that window, across unrelated subvolumes.

Reproduced 2026-08-24 against the live DB:
  snapshot id 1344 = /mnt/backup-22tb/projects/ClaudeCodeProjects-cloudflare-manager.20260517T2014
  'btrdasd list' on it returns audiobook content — 'Library/Stephen King/11-22-63: A Novel/...'
  span-model file count for that one project snapshot: 3,637,016

The span representation itself is sound (ranges are fragmented, e.g. 5-81, 92-93, 110-110, so discontinuity IS encoded). The defect is purely the missing scope predicate on read: nothing ties a span to the subvolume series it was recorded from.

Affects two of the three read commands — 'btrdasd list' returns contents that are not in the snapshot, and 'btrdasd search' attributes files to snapshots that never contained them. Anyone using either to decide what to restore, or to confirm a file was backed up, is reading fiction.
design: Options: (a) add a source/series column to spans and predicate on it, (b) allocate snapshot ids per-series, (c) join through snapshots and constrain on the series key. (a) or (c) preserve existing ids; (b) would require a migration of every existing row.
acceptance_criteria: btrdasd list on a project snapshot returns only that project's files and a plausible count; a span cannot match a snapshot from a different source; a regression test asserts cross-source non-matching against a fixture with interleaved snapshot ids.
notes:
Found while scoping a content-purge feature (rt6) — a purge must first ask 'which snapshots contain this path', which is precisely this broken query. Distinct from cu8 (dangling rows for deleted snapshots): cu8 is stale data, this is wrong data about live snapshots.

CORRECTION 2026-08-24, after reading the code: the original description claimed 'btrdasd search attributes files to snapshots that never contained them'. That is WRONG and the issue scope is narrower. search() never performs the id-range containment join — it reports each span's own first_snap/last_snap endpoints, and spans were verified series-coherent (0 of 85,038,167 spans have endpoints in different series). Only get_files_in_snapshot, get_files_in_snapshot_paged and count_files_in_snapshot carry the defect, i.e. 'btrdasd list' and any paginated listing built on it.

What search DOES suffer from is a separate defect: files.path is UNIQUE and relative-within-snapshot, so the same relative path in different subvolumes shares one files row and its size/mtime are clobbered on upsert. Filed separately.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.7.13.0, verified live on the installed binary 2026-08-24. btrdasd list on /mnt/backup-22tb/projects/ClaudeCodeProjects-cloudflare-manager.20260517T2014 now returns 265 files, all cloudflare-manager content, 0 audiobook rows — against 3,637,016 files and Stephen King audiobooks before. Read-path fix only: spans verified series-coherent (0 of 85,038,167 incoherent), so no migration or reindex. 4 of 5 regression tests confirmed red against the pre-fix query.

title: setup --upgrade silently refuses to regenerate btrbk.conf after any prior upgrade
description:
The bd-2lj staleness guard in setup/installer.rs skips ANY generated file whose on-disk mtime exceeds the btrdasd binary's. Its justification is sound only for the three include_str! scripts (backup-run.sh, backup-verify.sh, boot-archive-cleanup.sh), whose content is fixed at build time. Every other generated file — btrbk.conf and all systemd units — is rendered from Config by render_btrbk_conf/render_systemd_*, so its content is a pure function of config.toml and never of the binary's vintage.

Consequence: a successful 'setup --upgrade' stamps btrbk.conf with now, which is newer than the binary, so the NEXT upgrade refuses to rewrite it. The guard fires exactly when there is a real config change to apply, and 'Upgrade complete' is printed regardless. Config edits become inert until the binary is rebuilt.

Observed live 2026-09-01: btrbk.conf mtime 2026-08-31 20:40:12 vs /usr/bin/btrdasd 20:37:43; adding a source to config.toml produced 'Kept existing /etc/btrbk/btrbk.conf' and an unchanged btrbk.conf.
acceptance_criteria: Guard applies only to include_str! embedded scripts. Unit test proves a config-derived file newer than the binary IS rewritten, and an embedded script newer than the binary is still skipped. Both tests observed RED with the fix reverted.
close_reason: Fixed in 7c8ecd0. templates::is_embedded_script() scopes the 2lj mtime guard to the three include_str! scripts; config-derived files (btrbk.conf, systemd units) are always rewritten. Falsified: upgrade_rewrites_a_config_derived_file_newer_than_the_binary observed RED with the fix reverted, while the two original 2lj tests stayed green. Verified on the production path by touching btrbk.conf to +1h and confirming setup --upgrade regenerated it with no 'Kept existing' line.

title: Back up /srv/VirtualMachines (nested subvolume, silently absent from backups)
description: `@srv/VirtualMachines` was created 2026-08-31 20:14 on sata_pool as a subvolume NESTED inside `@srv`. It holds win11pro.qcow2 (34 GiB used, 137 GB virtual). btrfs send does not descend into nested subvolumes, so the daily `srv.<TS>` stream carries an EMPTY directory at that path — the backup succeeds and contains nothing. Proven: a read-only snapshot of /srv shows 0 bytes at VirtualMachines/ while the live path holds the 137 GB image.
acceptance_criteria: A dedicated source block exists in config.toml; btrbk.conf carries the subvolume; a real run lands a non-empty VirtualMachines subvolume on the 22TB target.
close_reason: PROVEN on the 22TB array. /mnt/backup-22tb/ssd-vm/srv-VirtualMachines.20260901T0041 holds win11pro.qcow2 at 36,219,510,784 bytes allocated (33.7 GiB) against 36,244,299,776 live -- the gap is the VM having run since the 00:41 snapshot. Received UUID 7f2b2433 is set, which only btrfs receive can do, so it is a genuine replica rather than a local copy, and the subvolume is readonly as a btrbk target should be. qemu-img check on the backed-up image: no errors, 84.07% allocated. Before the fix the same path inside an @srv snapshot was 0 bytes. Source ssd-vm scoped to primary-22tb only, per the ssd-steam precedent.

title: config.toml declares ClaudeCodeProjects/Asus-DarkHero, which no longer exists on disk
description: The subvolume ClaudeCodeProjects/Asus-DarkHero was deleted after 2026-08-31 13:59 (btrbk snapshotted it at 20260831T1359, and it is absent now). config.toml still declares it as a backup source, so the generated btrbk.conf still lists it. btrbk then emits 'Skipping subvolume ... No such file or directory' and exits nonzero. run_btrbk() records that as record_op btrbk FAIL, so the emailed report will say the backup FAILED even though every other subvolume backed up correctly. The run still exits 0 per the bd 18p split, so systemd stays green and sentinel will not thrash. This is a recurrence of bd DAS-Backup-Manager-vuw, which the run_btrbk() comment already documents as 'a stale source entry in config.toml made this a real, reproducible failure until the config was fixed'. Two orphaned snapshots of the deleted subvolume remain under ClaudeCodeProjects/.btrbk-snapshots/ (20260829T0322, 20260831T1359) and will age out under retention. NOTE: whether to remove the entry is the operator's call -- if Asus-DarkHero is coming back, the entry should stay and the false FAIL tolerated until then.
acceptance_criteria: Either the [[source.subvolumes]] entry for ClaudeCodeProjects/Asus-DarkHero is removed from config.toml and btrbk.conf regenerated, or the subvolume is recreated. Proven by a backup run whose report shows btrbk OK.
close_reason: Already resolved by a concurrent session: the [[source.subvolumes]] entry for ClaudeCodeProjects/Asus-DarkHero is gone from /etc/das-backup/config.toml and the regenerated /etc/btrbk/btrbk.conf (grep count 0). Operator confirmed the project is gone for good. CORRECTION to this issue's original text and to .claude/rules/backup.md: btrbk does NOT continue with rc=0 on a missing declared subvolume -- measured in isolation (config whose only defect was a missing subvolume), btrbk dryrun and btrbk list snapshots BOTH exit 10, which run_btrbk() records as btrbk FAIL. The report would have said FAILED, not merely warned. backup.md corrected with the measurement.

title: Rust backup path has no equivalent of verify_targets_before_btrbk (bd 9on reachable from the GUI)
description: scripts/backup-run.sh gained verify_targets_before_btrbk after the bd 9on incident (btrbk wrote to a bare mountpoint and filled the NVMe root). The Rust path has no equivalent. mount.rs sets any_available = true even on a failed bind mount, and run_backup deliberately skips the re-check when targets are explicitly specified -- which the GUI ALWAYS does. So the 9on failure mode is fully reachable from the GUI and from btrdasd with explicit targets.
acceptance_criteria: Rust asserts mountpoint + filesystem identity (UUID or serial) for every available target before invoking btrbk, on every path including explicitly-specified targets; falsified by pointing a target at a bare directory and observing refusal.
close_reason: Fixed: mount::verify_write_targets() runs before btrbk on every path including explicit-targets and dry-run, asserting mountpoint + expected filesystem UUID. Also corrected two ensure_targets_mounted branches that set any_available=true on failure. Four counter-tests, two observed RED with both positive controls green. NOTE: the any_available correction itself has no unit test -- it is defence in depth behind the tested guard.

title: restore_snapshot does not verify the snapshot argument lies under a configured target mount
description: restore_snapshot accepts a snapshot path from the caller and copies it as root into the destination. The destination is now constrained (allowed_roots + RESTORE_DENIED_ROOTS + O_NOFOLLOW, bd s05), but the SOURCE is not: an authorized caller can have root copy ANY directory tree on the host into an allowed root. Exfiltration primitive: copy /etc or /root into /home and read it unprivileged.
acceptance_criteria: snapshot is resolved and required to lie under one of the configured target mount points; a path outside them is refused before any read; counter-test copies from /etc and is refused.
close_reason: Fixed: check_source_allowed() requires the snapshot to resolve inside a configured backup target before anything is read; fails closed on an empty target list; snapshot_source_roots() admits both the configured mount and the live udisks2 mount. Three counter-tests, two observed RED against pre-fix code with the positive control staying green.

title: Index* D-Bus methods accept a caller-supplied db_path and open it as root
description: The Index* D-Bus methods take db_path from the caller and open it with root privilege. Polkit authorizes the ACTION, never the PATH, so an authorized caller chooses which file root opens/creates/writes as a SQLite database. Same shape as bd wd7, which was fixed for config_path by pinning CANONICAL_CONFIG but was never applied to db_path. Found during the nsp fail-silent audit as an out-of-scope observation.
acceptance_criteria: db_path is pinned to the canonical location (or validated against config) in every D-Bus Index* entry point; a caller-supplied path outside it is refused; test falsifies by attempting a write outside the canonical dir.
close_reason: Fixed: db_path parameter removed from all 7 Index* D-Bus methods; the helper resolves it from general.db_path in the canonical config via canonical_db_path(). GUI updated (7 classes de-plumbed, --db option and DatabasePath settings field removed rather than left inert). GUI builds clean under -Werror.

title: restore: traversal guard fails open on canonicalize error; dest entirely unvalidated
description:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-27 from ultrareview merged_bug_005, severity re-rated against installed polkit.

CODE (restore.rs, verified by reading it):
  (a) FAIL-OPEN GUARD: 'if let Ok(canonical_src) = src.canonicalize() && !canonical_src.starts_with(snapshot_path)'. The guard only fires when canonicalize returns Ok. It returns Err for a broken symlink, EACCES on any component, or a missing intermediate — precisely the cases an attacker-planted symlink exercises. On Err control falls through to symlink_metadata, the is_symlink arm runs, and std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&target, &dest_file) recreates the caller-controlled target.
  (b) UNVALIDATED DEST: std::fs::create_dir_all(dest) runs on the raw caller string; std::fs::copy(&src, &dest_file) follows destination symlinks. No allowlist, no O_NOFOLLOW.
  (c) snapshot_path is compared UN-canonicalized against a canonicalized src, so on udisks2 mounts (/run/media/... vs /mnt/...) legitimate restores are spuriously blocked. This is an availability bug independent of the security ones.

POLKIT: org.dasbackup.restore = auth_admin_keep (verified in the installed policy). So this needs admin authentication — the review's 'polkit-authorized caller plants a systemd unit' is real but requires admin credentials, not merely an active session. Reviewer was too alarming on reachability; the code defects are exactly as described.
design: (a) canonicalize snapshot_path ONCE at entry and compare against that; on src.canonicalize() Err, push an error and continue rather than falling through. (b) canonicalize dest and require it under an allowlist; open the write target with O_NOFOLLOW|O_EXCL instead of fs::copy so a pre-planted dest symlink fails the open. (c) fixes itself once snapshot_path is canonicalized.
acceptance_criteria: A broken symlink in a snapshot is REFUSED, not recreated — observed. A dest outside the allowlist is refused. A restore via a udisks2 mount path succeeds (regression for (c)).
close_reason: Fixed in 0.7.20.0. 388 unit tests + 2 root-gated loopback tests green; clippy clean; every new test observed RED against mutated code. Live-verified on the production host after deploy: wd7 (ConfigGet 0-arg works, old 1-arg form rejected 'Signature mismatch'), dca (lock free -> btrbk ran, 49 snapshots; lock genuinely held -> no btrbk process at all), s05 (/etc refused by denylist, /srv refused by allowlist, /tmp succeeded with correct content). 5ig verified by loopback falsification plus live confirmation of the naming premise: production btrbk wrote '.btrbk-snapshots/root-.20260828T0747', the hyphenated name the old hardcoded prefix could never match.

title: config_path is caller-supplied on 17 D-Bus methods — unprompted root file read via config.read
description:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-27 from ultrareview bug_025, with severity RE-RATED after reading the installed polkit policy.

CODE: load_config (btrdasd-helper.rs:274) and save_config (:279) pass the caller's string straight to Config::load/save. 17 interface methods take config_path: &str. No canonicalize, no allowlist — grep for canonicalize/allowlist/starts_with in the helper returns only one unrelated hit (parsing systemd timer output).

POLKIT (verified in the INSTALLED /usr/share/polkit-1/actions/org.dasbackup.policy, not assumed):
  org.dasbackup.config.read -> allow_active=YES (no prompt)
  org.dasbackup.config      -> auth_admin_keep (admin password)

SO THE TWO HALVES DIFFER SHARPLY, and the review conflated them:
  READ (config_get:1136, schedule_get:1176 — both check config.read): REAL and UNPROMPTED. Any active local session reads any TOML-parseable file with root's privileges, no authentication. This is the half that matters.
  WRITE (config_set:1151, schedule_set:1202 + the subvol mutators — all check config): requires admin auth, so the reviewer's '/etc/systemd/system overwrite by any local user' scenario does NOT hold. Still worth fixing as privilege-boundary hygiene, and auth_admin_KEEP caches the grant for the session, so one legitimate admin config edit leaves a window where further calls do not re-prompt.

The reviewer was too alarming on the write half and correct on the read half.
design: Drop config_path from every interface method and hardcode the canonical /etc/das-backup/config.toml server-side — the daemon already treats it as canonical (helper opens exactly that path in its pre-warm task). If multi-config is ever needed, match against an explicit allowlist.
acceptance_criteria: config_get against a path outside the canonical location is refused — observed. Counter-test: the canonical path still works.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.7.20.0. 388 unit tests + 2 root-gated loopback tests green; clippy clean; every new test observed RED against mutated code. Live-verified on the production host after deploy: wd7 (ConfigGet 0-arg works, old 1-arg form rejected 'Signature mismatch'), dca (lock free -> btrbk ran, 49 snapshots; lock genuinely held -> no btrbk process at all), s05 (/etc refused by denylist, /srv refused by allowlist, /tmp succeeded with correct content). 5ig verified by loopback falsification plus live confirmation of the naming premise: production btrbk wrote '.btrbk-snapshots/root-.20260828T0747', the hyphenated name the old hardcoded prefix could never match.

title: D-Bus helper takes no maintenance/singleton lock — pe6 fix never reached the GUI path
description:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-27 from ultrareview bug_024. btrdasd-helper.rs contains ZERO lock references (/usr/bin/grep for acquire_manual_locks|FileLock|flock|maintenance|das-backup.lock returns nothing). backup_run goes check_polkit -> load_config -> spawn_blocking -> ensure_sources_mounted -> ensure_targets_mounted -> run_backup -> unmount, with no lock anywhere. Same for backup_snapshot/backup_send/backup_boot_archive.

THIS IS pe6 LEFT HALF-DONE. pe6 ('Manual btrdasd backup subcommands take no maintenance lock') was filed 2026-08-02 and closed 2026-08-25 as 'Fixed in 0.7.15.0, VERIFIED live'. That fix wired main.rs (4 call sites: 1547/1610/1627/1648) into the two-lock scheme. The D-Bus helper — the GUI's entire backup path — was never touched. pe6's own description names the hazard verbatim: 'doctor mounts a source; a concurrent manual backup sees it already mounted and uses it unregistered; doctor finishes first and unmounts it mid-use.'

REVIEWER'S SUPPORTING FACT WAS WRONG, headline still right: bug_024 claimed acquire_manual_locks is 'reachable ONLY from its own two unit tests'. False — main.rs calls it at four sites. The true statement is narrower and still serious: the helper does not call it.

IMPACT: a GUI 'Run Backup' click can run concurrently with the 03:00 timer, with a running scrub (which holds the maintenance lock for hours), or with a second GUI backup. MountGuard::Drop can unmount a target out from under a live btrfs receive.
design: Wrap each of the four helper backup handlers' spawn_blocking body in backup::acquire_manual_locks, mapping AlreadyRunning to a job_finished('declined') signal so the GUI shows the skip rather than a phantom job that silently did nothing. Reuse the existing main.rs pattern verbatim.
acceptance_criteria: With /run/das-backup.lock held, a GUI/D-Bus backup_run declines instead of proceeding — observed, not reasoned. Counter-test: with the lock free it proceeds normally.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.7.20.0. 388 unit tests + 2 root-gated loopback tests green; clippy clean; every new test observed RED against mutated code. Live-verified on the production host after deploy: wd7 (ConfigGet 0-arg works, old 1-arg form rejected 'Signature mismatch'), dca (lock free -> btrbk ran, 49 snapshots; lock genuinely held -> no btrbk process at all), s05 (/etc refused by denylist, /srv refused by allowlist, /tmp succeeded with correct content). 5ig verified by loopback falsification plus live confirmation of the naming premise: production btrbk wrote '.btrbk-snapshots/root-.20260828T0747', the hyphenated name the old hardcoded prefix could never match.

title: Triage ultrareview findings from PR #42 (privilege boundary, 7 files)
description:
PR #42 is a synthetic Recipe C review PR (base review-base-privboundary at root commit, head review-head-privboundary) covering 7 files / 7721 lines read in full: btrdasd-helper.rs, backup.rs, restore.rs, mount.rs, subvol.rs, setup/templates.rs, scripts/backup-run.sh. Chosen as one complete privilege boundary from the unprivileged D-Bus surface down to btrfs subvolume delete. This consumes the last /ultrareview credit, so findings are non-renewable — capture all of them here.

Priority 1 in the PR body is the fail-silent audit (2>/dev/null, || true, .ok(), unwrap_or(default)) that has been deferred five-plus times since 2026-08-25; this PR is the vehicle for finally getting it done.
design:
Review provenance (PR #42 now CLOSED, branches deleted — findings survive as a PR comment).
  base review-base-privboundary = 308e0c43f546471d9d18481c2cc37cdf25c48476 (root commit)
  head review-head-privboundary = b090205ae9ad684d1c74b333ec572ee472b3da65
Reviewed exactly: backup.rs, bin/btrdasd-helper.rs, restore.rs, mount.rs, subvol.rs, setup/templates.rs, scripts/backup-run.sh (7 files, +7721/-0, all status=added).
Verified 2026-08-27 before closing: those 7 files were byte-identical between b090205 and main, so all file:line citations in the findings map onto main with zero offset. If main drifts before a finding is triaged, re-anchor against b090205 via: git diff b090205 main -- <file>
acceptance_criteria: Every finding recorded here verbatim; each independently verified per ULTRAREVIEW-HOWTO section 12 (re-derive from source, chase every hedge, test stated impact end-to-end, re-rate severity yourself) before any code change; real defects split into their own issues; PR #42 closed and review-base-privboundary / review-head-privboundary deleted from origin and locally.
notes:
VERIFICATION COMPLETE 2026-08-27 — all 10 findings independently re-derived from source, live config, and the INSTALLED polkit policy. None taken on the reviewer's word.

RESULT: 10/10 are real code defects. 1 is not reachable on this host. 4 carried inaccurate supporting facts.

Split into: 5ig (P0), dca (P1), wd7 (P1), s05 (P1), stream_command deadlock (P2), job_cancel (P2), nit cluster (P3).

CORRECTIONS TO THE REVIEW (all four erred in a direction that mattered):
1. bug_024 said acquire_manual_locks is 'reachable ONLY from its own two unit tests'. FALSE — main.rs calls it at 1547/1610/1627/1648. The true and still-serious statement: the D-Bus HELPER never calls it. Reviewer too alarming on the fact, right on the headline. Extra context the review lacked: this is bd pe6 left half-done — pe6 was closed 2026-08-25 as 'VERIFIED live' after fixing main.rs only.
2. bug_025 treated read and write as one finding. Installed polkit splits them sharply: config.read = allow_active=YES (unprompted — the read primitive is REAL), config = auth_admin_keep (the '/etc overwrite by any local user' scenario does NOT hold). Reviewer too alarming on the write half.
3. merged_bug_005 likewise: org.dasbackup.restore = auth_admin_keep, so admin credentials are required. Code defects exactly as described; reachability overstated.
4. merged_bug_020 cited templates.rs:745-773, which is TEST code — the parsers are at :576 and :585. And it is unreachable here: the only caller is render_cron_entry under InitSystem::Sysvinit|Openrc, while live config has system = 'systemd'.
5. bug_023 said three mkdir sites discard status; it is two (417, 431) of five.

FINDING THE REVIEW MISSED, on its own top finding: merged_bug_004's failure is ASYMMETRIC. @home maps to snap_name 'home', btrbk.conf:31 is plain 'home', so nvme/home.<TS> matches and @home IS recreated correctly. Only @ is destroyed, because btrbk.conf:28 is 'root-' (disambiguated against 'root-root' at :34) while the Rust prefix is 'nvme/root.'. Proven with a standalone Rust program using the real strings.

ALSO: the review's proposed fix for merged_bug_004 (derive names from templates.rs::resolve_snapshot_names) would rebuild the very two-implementations problem the bug IS. Correct approach is btrdasd forget's precedent — read /etc/btrbk/btrbk.conf, the file btrbk itself consumes.

title: Production index has ~15M spans referencing snapshot ids that do not exist — blocks reconcile
description:
The live backup-index.db violates its own FOREIGN KEY constraints, and has done since before 2026-08-24.

Measured on /var/lib/das-backup/backup-index.db:
  14,827,694 spans with a dangling first_snap  (17.4% of 85,038,167)
  14,984,318 spans with a dangling last_snap
  57 distinct missing snapshot ids referenced
  snapshots.id runs 1..6579 but holds only 6515 rows — 64 ids absent from the sequence, in clusters (104-107, 110-115, ...)

PRE-EXISTING, not caused by the 0.7.13.x work: the byte-identical counts are present in the pre-change backup taken before any reconcile ran (backup-index.db.pre-0.7.13.0-20260824-230822). db.rs:133 sets PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, so these rows cannot have been written by a connection this binary opened — a non-enforcing writer, an older schema, or an interrupted migration is implied. Cause unknown.

Why it blocks reconcile (cu8): prune re-inserts repaired spans, and an INSERT re-validates foreign keys on the row. A span whose last_snap was ALREADY dangling is tolerated as legacy data but REJECTED when rewritten, so the pass aborts with SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY (787). Observed live: 'btrdasd reconcile' ran ~10 minutes against the 85M-span index and rolled back cleanly, index byte-identical. The 5814 stale snapshot rows therefore remain.

Note these spans are already unreachable by the read path after 5uq: get_files_in_snapshot JOINs snapshots on first_snap, so a dangling start matches nothing. They are dead weight AND constraint violations.
design: Deleting them is defensible — a span referencing a nonexistent snapshot can never match a query and cannot be rewritten — but it is ~15M rows and a data repair with its own risk profile, materially different from 'prune snapshots that no longer exist'. Held for an explicit decision rather than bundled into the cu8 remediation. Whatever runs it should also make reconcile fail with a diagnosed message rather than a raw SqliteFailure.
acceptance_criteria: PRAGMA foreign_key_check on the production index returns no rows; btrdasd reconcile completes and prunes the 5814 stale snapshots; a decision is recorded on whether reconcile deletes dangling spans itself or a separate repair does it.
notes: Found 2026-08-24 while remediating the live index after the 0.7.13.x release. Prod is SAFE and untouched: 6515 snapshots / 85,038,167 spans, PRAGMA integrity_check ok, targets unmounted, locks free. Rollback copy retained at the .pre-0.7.13.0- path.
close_reason:
FIXED and verified live 2026-08-25 via btrdasd reconcile --repair (0.7.16.0+). Removed 15,085,764 dangling spans and 271 orphaned files from the production index; PRAGMA foreign_key_check now returns ZERO rows and integrity_check is ok, against 14,827,694 dangling first_snap + 14,984,318 dangling last_snap before. Spans went 85,038,167 -> 69,952,403.

Resolved surgically rather than by the full reindex originally chosen: the rebuild proved impractical at this data size (see 3sa — measured at 670 files/min by 4.3M rows, roughly 13 days extrapolated), so it was stopped at 204 of ~1300 snapshots and the index restored intact from backup before the surgical path was taken. Deleting these rows is sound because they are unreachable after 5uq — the read path joins snapshots on first_snap, so a dangling start matches nothing — and they are live FK violations that cannot be rewritten at all while foreign_keys=ON.

Covered by two tests: one builds the production shape (a span whose last_snap names a deleted snapshot), asserts the repair removes exactly it plus its orphaned file, leaves healthy spans untouched, stops search serving the removed path, AND proves the previously-refused prune then succeeds; the other asserts a clean index is left unchanged.

title: btrdasd purge <path> — remove unwanted content from existing backups and the index
description:
There is currently no way to remove specific content from backups once written. The need is real and sometimes urgent: a credential or key that got snapshotted, PII, or bulk data backed up by mistake. Today the only recourse is deleting whole snapshots by hand across every target, with the index left asserting the content still exists.

HARD CONSTRAINT — in-place file deletion inside a backup is impossible and must never be attempted. Target snapshots are received read-only subvolumes; removing a file requires clearing ro, which permanently destroys the Received UUID (only btrfs receive can set it). Per .claude/rules/backup.md that leaves 'a subvolume that looks like a valid replica while its content may drift', and silently disqualifies it as an incremental parent. Mutating an already-sent LOCAL parent is equally unsafe: btrfs send -p diffs against it and never re-emits what the target is missing.

Therefore the only sound implementation is content-targeted but SNAPSHOT-GRANULAR:
  1. Resolve every snapshot containing the path, via the index (requires 5uq fixed — today that query is wrong).
  2. Show a dry-run plan: affected snapshots per target, reclaimed bytes, and which retention tiers are lost.
  3. Remove the path from the live source subvolume.
  4. Delete the affected snapshots wholesale on source and all targets (btrfs subvolume delete only).
  5. Prune the corresponding index rows (see cu8), so search stops serving the purged path.
  6. Next run re-sends the affected series in full — must be stated up front in the dry-run, since it is the real cost.

Note the DB layer is already half-built for step 5: the schema carries files_ad and files_au triggers that maintain files_fts on DELETE/UPDATE of files, but no Rust code ever issues a DELETE — the delete path was anticipated in SQL and never implemented in the API.

NON-GOAL, permanently: removing a file while keeping the snapshot that contained it. Anyone who needs that wants a different backup topology, not this command.
design: Depends on 5uq (span source scoping) because step 1 is exactly that query, and on cu8 (index prune) for step 5. Without 5uq the command would delete the wrong snapshots — a data-loss bug, not a cosmetic one, so 5uq is a hard prerequisite rather than a nice-to-have.
acceptance_criteria: btrdasd purge --dry-run lists every affected snapshot per target, bytes reclaimed, retention tiers lost, and states the resulting full re-send; purge removes the path from the live source, deletes affected snapshots via btrfs subvolume delete on source and all targets, and prunes index rows so btrdasd search returns zero hits for the purged path; ro is never cleared on any subvolume; role=mirror targets' independent OS subvolumes are never in scope.
notes: Requested by the user 2026-08-24 after the claude-cowork-linux rename cleanup, having been told the in-place variant is architecturally impossible. Filed as the snapshot-granular design, which is the achievable form of the request.
close_reason: Shipped in 0.7.16.0, VERIFIED live: 'btrdasd purge *PKGBUILD --dry-run' matched snapshots across six series INCLUDING the live ClaudeCodeProjects-claude-cowork-desktop-maintenance — demonstrating the deliberate absence of a live-series guard, which is the whole point since purging a leaked secret means touching the series still being backed up. Whole-snapshot granularity is the only sound option and the command says so, along with the restore points lost and the full re-send that follows: a file cannot be removed from a received read-only subvolume without clearing ro, which permanently destroys the Received UUID only btrfs receive can set. Scoping uses Database::snapshots_containing(), series-scoped so a purge can never delete the wrong snapshots.

title: Index never prunes rows for deleted snapshots — search serves nonexistent snapshots as current
description:
db.rs (1092 lines) has no delete/prune/vacuum path and indexer.rs has no reconciliation for vanished snapshots: the API is append-and-query only. Every snapshot reaped by btrbk retention, or deleted manually, leaves its rows in backup-index.db permanently.

Measured 2026-08-24 on /var/lib/das-backup/backup-index.db:
  - /mnt/backup-22tb/projects/: 2871 index rows vs 327 subvolumes on disk = 2544 dangling (89%)
  - 6515 snapshot rows total in the index

User-facing impact (this is the part that matters): 'btrdasd search PKGBUILD' returns a hit with span ClaudeCodeProjects-claude-cowork-linux.20260802T1605 -> .20260824T0316. The first was reaped by retention weeks ago; the last was deleted 2026-08-24. Search presents both as current locations of the file. A restore attempt against either path fails at the filesystem.

This is the verification.md section 3 'consumer with no producer' shape: the index serves data nothing maintains, with no signal that it is stale.
acceptance_criteria: btrdasd walk (or a dedicated reconcile pass) removes snapshot rows whose path no longer exists on disk, cascading to files/spans; search returns zero hits in nonexistent snapshots; existing 2544 dangling rows on this host are cleaned up.
notes:
UNBLOCKED as of 2026-08-25: opd is fixed, the index carries zero FK violations, and prune_snapshots no longer refuses.

Still open on the remediation itself. The live prune of 5814 stale snapshot rows was started and ran 62 minutes without completing, holding the maintenance lock while the 03:04 backup queued behind it (deferring correctly). It was stopped so the backup could run; being one transaction it rolled back cleanly, leaving the repair committed and the index at 6515 snapshots / 69,952,403 spans, integrity ok.

The slow phase is span repair: with 5814 of 6515 snapshots doomed, nearly every span needs its endpoints recomputed via a correlated subquery. Same root cause as 3sa. Do NOT simply re-run it in a window that overlaps a backup — either fix the performance first, or run it immediately after a backup completes with hours of clear headroom.
close_reason:
COMPLETE and verified live 2026-08-25. After reconcile --repair cleared the FK blocker (opd), the auto-reconcile inside btrdasd walk finished the remediation during the scheduled backup: 5861 stale snapshots pruned, 22,713,781 spans repaired, 23,158,421 removed, 5,919,536 files dropped.

Acceptance met exactly: btrdasd search returns ZERO hits for the claude-cowork-linux snapshots deleted 2026-08-24 (24 index rows before, 0 now), and a follow-up reconcile --dry-run reports Confirmed present 610, Stale 0, Skipped 0 — the index is consistent with disk. Final state 610 snapshots / 18,888,326 spans / 15,521,936 files, integrity ok, foreign_key_check zero rows.

Note for future work: the delivery mechanism was the in-walk reconcile, not the standalone command. A standalone prune of the same backlog ran 62 minutes without completing while holding the maintenance lock; inside a backup it had the hours it needed. Span repair over a large doomed set is slow — see 3sa.

title: BTRFS read errors on all DAS drives — sdi1=179, sdl1=227, sdj2=258 — likely USB/enclosure
description:

  /dev/sdl1 (22TB leg 2, ZXA1R71M):  227 read errors
  /dev/sdj2 (2TB recovery-A, ZK208Q77): 258 read errors

dmesg confirms: 'BTRFS error (device sdiN): bdev /dev/sdiN errs: wr 0, rd N, flush 0, corrupt 0, gen 0' messages for sdi1, sdl1, sdj2.

That walk hit fs::read_dir → kernel did the retry → eventually surfaced as 'Indexing target failed (non-fatal): Input/output error (os error 5)' for all three targets. The actual btrbk send/receive succeeded (45 created, 2 sent, ALL OPERATIONS SUCCESSFUL email) because that's a more retry-tolerant code path.

Hypothesis (most → least likely):
1. USB cable degraded — affects multiple drives simultaneously through the same bus
2. TerraMaster D6-320 enclosure power supply / backplane issue
3. USB hub or controller chip overheating
4. One drive's surface degrading and the SATA error cascade is hitting peers
5. Kernel-level btrfs/usb-storage bug

Recommended next steps:
1. Stop and unmount cleanly: 'sudo umount /run/media/bosco/das-backup-22tb*' and '/mnt/backup-22tb' if present
2. Run 'btrfs scrub start /run/media/bosco/das-backup-22tb' (and the recovery mounts) to map out which extents the errors hit — about 8-12h wall over USB for 22TB array

4. Power-cycle the DAS enclosure to clear any transient USB state
5. If errors persist after power-cycle + scrub clean: replace the USB cable (cheapest probable fix)

title: backup-run.sh writes to bare mountpoint dir on / when DAS target is not mounted
description:
Failure mode (observed in May 2026): the original 22TB DAS disk (ZXA0LMAE) was physically removed for replacement. The second leg of the new RAID-1 pair (ZXA1NYGZ) was present. backup-run.sh ran on its normal schedule and — instead of refusing to back up to an unmounted target OR mounting the remaining leg in degraded mode — wrote to /mnt/backup-22tb as a regular directory on / (the NVMe root filesystem). This filled / and forced urgent cleanup.

ROOT CAUSE CLASS: classic Unix foot-gun. /mnt/backup-22tb exists as a directory whether or not the DAS filesystem is mounted on it. If btrbk (or its parent script) doesn't verify that the destination is a real mountpoint backed by the EXPECTED filesystem (by UUID/label/device-serial), the operation succeeds in writing — but it writes to /, not to the DAS.

Required fix:
1. Before invoking btrbk for any DAS target, verify that:
   a. The destination IS a mountpoint (mountpoint -q OR findmnt -T)
   b. The mounted filesystem has the EXPECTED label/UUID from config.toml
   c. (Belt-and-suspenders) The underlying block device serial matches a configured DAS drive
2. If any check fails, ABORT before writing a single byte.
3. Emit a clear error explaining what was expected vs. found, and which DAS serial(s) the target requires.

Belongs in scripts/backup-run.sh. Same guard should run for every target in config.toml (primary-22tb, system-2tb, system-mirror-2tb), not just the 22TB primary. The 'degraded' mount option already configured for the RAID-1 primary means a single-leg failure should still successfully mount — the bug is that when zero legs are present, the script falls through to writing to /.

Severity: P1 — caused real outage on /, forced cleanup work, and could trivially recur if a DAS drive fails or is unplugged again.
close_reason: Implemented and verified 2026-05-12. scripts/backup-run.sh v4.2.2 adds two defense layers: create_mount_points now refuses to mkdir bare mountpoints for unavailable targets and rmdirs empty ones (aborts on non-empty leak evidence); new verify_targets_before_btrbk function asserts every configured target is either a real mountpoint backed by the expected UUID/serial OR does not exist on disk, aborting with per-target violation listing otherwise. Embedded into btrdasd via include_str!, rebuilt and reinstalled. Verified: live happy-path with 3 mounted targets + 4-test unit harness covering all failure paths. shellcheck clean.

Each timeout consumes ~1h 32min CPU + 108G memory peak per journal record. btrfs subprocess survives initial SIGTERM; requires final SIGKILL. The das-backup.service unit then enters 'failed' state, and /mnt/backup-22tb is left unmounted.

Hardware state at time of regression:
- Original 22TB drive (Seagate ST22000NM000C, serial ZXA0LMAE) physically removed and RMA'd.
- Replacement drive (ST22000NM000C, serial ZXA1NYGZ) installed, all SMART counters clean.

btrbk relies on parent-snapshot UUIDs on the destination to perform incremental btrfs send. With the destination FS replaced (different UUID, no carried-over snapshots), btrbk cannot find a parent for any source subvolume — every source is being sent in full. 1. Inspect /etc/btrbk/btrbk.conf and confirm 'incremental yes' is configured; check the run with 'btrbk --verbose --dry-run run' or similar to see what btrbk plans for each subvolume.
2. Confirm via journal/btrbk output whether the failed runs are attempting full sends (look for 'send (full)' vs 'send (incremental)').
3. If confirmed initial-full-send: complete the seed once manually with TimeoutSec=infinity (or 24h), then subsequent runs are normal incrementals well under the 6h budget.
4. Alternative: seed parent snapshots on the destination FS via 'btrfs send --no-data' or by copying small recent snapshots out-of-band before the first scheduled run.
5. Consider whether das-backup.service.TimeoutSec should be raised permanently for safety (e.g., 12h), with a separate watchdog/alert if a run actually runs that long.

title: das-backup: RAID-1 backup targets must survive drive failure (multi-serial + FS-UUID mount)
description:
The current Target schema (serial: String, scalar) defeats the reliability promise of using RAID-1 for backup targets. When any single RAID-1 partner becomes unavailable (failed, dying, evicted, mid-replacement), find_device_by_serial() in scripts/backup-run.sh returns empty for the configured serial → script logs 'Primary backup drive not found' → exits with no backups written. The remaining healthy leg of the RAID-1 array is fully mountable in degraded mode and could continue serving backups, but the script never tries.

This is the exact opposite of what RAID-1 exists to provide. The whole point of putting backups on a RAID-1 array is that one drive can die without anyone noticing operationally. Currently the backup silently stops the moment that scenario happens.

Discovered 2026-05-07 during the ZXA0LMAE → RMA workflow: had to manually edit /etc/das-backup/config.toml to point the primary-22tb target at the surviving partner (ZXA1NYGZ) before the backup script could find any device. Without that edit, post-eviction the daily backup would have silently stopped.

Affected source: indexer/src/config.rs (Target struct), indexer/src/setup/env_export.rs, scripts/backup-run.sh (find_device_by_serial + mount_sources).
design:
Two-field redesign:

1. Mount identity (the WHAT-to-mount) — use the BTRFS filesystem UUID, not a device path. BTRFS auto-discovers all members from any single member's superblock once 'btrfs device scan' has run (which udev does at hot-plug). New field:
     mount_uuid: String   (or alternatively: mount_label, mount_partuuid)
   This field is stable across drive swaps, partner additions, and degraded mode.

2. Expected-membership (the WHAT-we-expected-to-find) — change serial: String → serials: Vec<String>. backup-run.sh logs warnings when expected serials are absent ('configured pair was [X, Y], only X present, running degraded'), but never aborts on absence. Useful operator signal without coupling availability to individual drives.

Backwards compatibility in the TOML parser:
- Accept legacy form: serial = "X"  → normalize to serials = ["X"]
- Accept new form: serials = ["X", "Y"]
- Eventually deprecate the legacy form in a major version

env_export.rs changes:
- Emit DAS_TARGET_<i>_SERIALS as a space-separated list (or _SERIAL_0, _SERIAL_1 indexed)
- Emit DAS_TARGET_<i>_MOUNT_UUID

backup-run.sh changes:
- mount_sources(): mount by 'UUID=<mount_uuid>' instead of resolving serial → /dev/sdX
- find_device_by_serial → find_devices_by_serials returning a list; warn on absences
- Keep the 'primary backup drive' health check but make it a warning, not an exit, when the *array* is reachable
acceptance_criteria:
Backup must succeed in all four operational states of a 2-leg RAID-1 target:

1. Both legs present + healthy → normal RAID-1 reads/writes
2. Only the originally-anchor leg present (partner failed) → mounts in degraded mode, writes succeed
3. Only the partner leg present (anchor failed) → mounts in degraded mode, writes succeed
4. Both present, but one in pre-failure (SMART warnings) → backup runs, log records SMART state

Tests must cover the schema migration:
- Old config (serial = "X") parses to Target { serials: vec!["X"], .. }
- New config (serials = ["X", "Y"]) parses correctly
- Mixed cases: only mount_uuid given (no serials) — backup-run.sh runs but emits 'no expected-serials list to verify membership' warning
- Round-trip: TOML → struct → TOML preserves data

Operational acceptance:
- Yanking the anchor drive from a live array does NOT stop the next backup run (verified on test-vm or by simulation)
- Restoring the anchor drive to its bay does NOT require a config edit
notes:
Implementation landed 2026-05-09 (in-tree + production):

CODE: Target struct gained serials: Vec<String> and mount_uuid: Option<String>. Legacy serial: String preserved for back-compat with health/SMART/GUI reads — auto-populated from serials[0] via From<TargetRaw> deserialization shim. validate() updated: a target needs ≥1 of {serial, serials, mount_uuid}. env_export.rs emits new DAS_TARGET_<i>_SERIALS (space-separated) and DAS_TARGET_<i>_MOUNT_UUID alongside legacy _SERIAL. backup-run.sh v4.2.0 reads SERIALS list, prefers mount-by-UUID (BTRFS auto-discovery from any present leg's superblock), warns-not-fails on per-serial absence, only aborts when ALL primary targets unreachable.

TESTS: 7 new (legacy-parse, new-list-parse, uuid-only-parse, mixed-prefers-serials, round-trip-strips-legacy, validate-uuid-only-passes, validate-no-anchor-fails). All 143 lib tests pass under release. cargo clippy -D warnings clean. shellcheck clean (one pre-existing SC2015 in unrelated email-send code). cargo fmt applied.

PRODUCTION: /etc/das-backup/config.toml primary-22tb migrated to serials = ["ZXA1NYGZ"] + mount_uuid = "46ffbd7c-..." (backup at config.toml.bak.20260509-110807-pre-multi-serial-uuid). New btrdasd installed to /usr/bin/btrdasd. New backup-run.sh installed to /usr/lib/das-backup/backup-run.sh. dump-env on production config now emits all new vars correctly.

ACCEPTANCE STATE:
✓ Schema migration: legacy + new + uuid-only TOML all parse, round-trip is canonical-form-only
✓ Backup proceeds when no expected serial present (UUID-resolvable)
✓ Backup proceeds when partial serials present (degraded warning only)
✓ Backwards compat: legacy serial='X' configs still work
⏸ Acceptance #1 (both legs healthy → normal RAID-1): blocked until replacement drive arrives. Will verify post-RMA.
⏸ Acceptance #4 (SMART warnings recorded): orthogonal feature, separate issue.

OPERATIONAL DISCOVERY (separate from schema bug): the live 22TB array is currently NOT writable-mountable in degraded mode. Cause: prior session's cancelled `btrfs balance dconvert=single` left ≥1 single-profile chunk and tree blocks allocated on the now-wiped ZXA0LMAE. `btrfs check --readonly` shows tree-block bytenr mismatches. Schema fix is correct and works, but THIS specific FS will require mkfs+rebuild from /hddRaid1/das-backup-22tb-rescue when the replacement drive arrives (btrfs replace cannot recover orphan-single chunks). File a separate issue for the rebuild runbook.

Verified done 2026-05-12 — was orphan in_progress, never closed. The multi-serial + mount-by-UUID redesign described in the design field is fully implemented:
- DAS_SERIALS_LIST array env-exported in templates: backup-run.sh:82 with legacy single-serial fallback (${!serials_var:-${!serial_var}})
- TARGET_MOUNT_UUIDS array: backup-run.sh:83
- check_das_connected uses both: line 234-264, with blkid -U UUID fallback (line 253-258) for the case where no configured serial matches but the FS UUID resolves on disk
- DAS_MOUNT_OPTS includes 'degraded' (confirmed in dump-env output 2026-05-12)
- backup-run.sh header line 10-12 explicitly cross-references this bd ID

Live proof: today's dryrun completed normally with one configured serial (ZXA1NYGZ) and UUID-based mount; verify_targets_before_btrbk logged 'primary-22tb: OK (/mnt/backup-22tb → UUID=b2dbe07d-...)' confirming UUID-path verification works in production.

title: doctor exit 1 on drift makes systemd+sentinel report a service failure, not a finding
description:
btrdasd doctor exits 1 when drift is FOUND, which is a successful check with a result. systemd marks das-backup-doctor.service failed; cachyos-sentinel then (a) restarts it, which fails identically, and (b) emits the desktop notification 'backup service das-backup-doctor.service last run failed: Result=exit-code'. The operator is told the checker broke when in fact it worked and has something to say — and the real signal (the drift email) arrives alongside a contradicting failure alert.

Evidence 2026-08-31: doctor ran 13:47:34, found ClaudeCodeProjects/powershell-scripts, emailed the report, exited 1. sentinel-core logged 'service in failed state' at 13:47:57, restarted it, logged 'service restart command failed', and notified at 13:48:08. Same double-start on Aug 23 (02:00:01 and 02:00:09). Bounded at 2 starts — sentinel gives up when the restart fails synchronously — so this is not the unbounded loop 18p guarded against.

This is the same distinction 18p drew for scrub: the PROCESS exit code should answer 'could the check run?', while 'what did it find?' travels by email/--json/report. ScrubPass::success() stayed the source of truth for the scrub FAILURE email while exit_code_for_pass() was narrowed to 'the pass could not even start'.

Counter-argument, which is why this is filed rather than fixed: exit 1 on drift is documented in the --help EXIT CODE text and is useful to scripts and CI. Changing it is a behaviour change for any external consumer, so it is the operator's call.
acceptance_criteria: Either the exit code is narrowed to run/could-not-run with the drift signal carried by email/--json (and the --help text plus .claude/rules updated), or a note records the deliberate decision to keep exit 1 and accept the sentinel notification.

title: Primary ESP has no named NVRAM entry — boot order resolved by firmware enumeration
description:
Verified 2026-08-31 after the motherboard swap (Crosshair VIII Dark Hero -> Hero, BIOS 5601). All four disk boot entries are firmware auto-created generics: every one is named `UEFI OS` and points at the removable-media fallback \\EFI\\BOOT\\BOOTX64.EFI. There is no `Linux Boot Manager` entry.

Consequence: boot selection is resolved by firmware enumeration order, and two of the four candidates are USB-attached bootable recovery disks whose device letters drift on every reconnect. Nothing pins the primary ESP to the head of BootOrder by identity.

Observed order: Boot0001 primary (PARTUUID ca1c0553-...), Boot0002 mirror (cc7834c1-...), Boot0003 bay-1 recovery (fe640619-...), Boot0004 bay-4 recovery (ef19ce6e-...). Those numbers are informational only — they are re-issued on any NVRAM reset.

Proposed remedy: `bootctl install` on /boot, creating a `Linux Boot Manager` entry resolved by partition GUID at the head of BootOrder, followed by one manual /usr/local/bin/esp-sync.sh run so the mirror picks up refreshed loader binaries.

OWNERSHIP: this is a bootloader change confined to the primary ESP (LABEL=EFI, /boot). Per ~/.claude/rules/esp-ownership.md 'Where the boundary actually falls', that belongs to CachyOS-Kernel, NOT to this project. DAS-Backup-Manager owns ESP partition lifecycle and all cross-ESP operations; it does not own boot configuration confined to /boot. This issue exists to track the handoff, not to authorise the work here.

MUST NOT happen as part of any fix: deleting Boot0002/0003/0004 (equivalents). They are the mirror failover and the two independent recovery-OS boot paths.

Not this project's to fix — handed to CachyOS-Kernel.

WHY CLOSED RATHER THAN FIXED: the remedy is 'bootctl install' on /boot — a bootloader change confined to the primary ESP (LABEL=EFI). ~/.claude/rules/esp-ownership.md 'Where the boundary actually falls' assigns that to CachyOS-Kernel. THE GAP IS REAL AND STILL OPEN ON THE HOST. title: das-partition-drives.sh would create BTRFS labels that match no drive on disk
description:
`partition_data_drive`/`partition_bootable_drive` build the BTRFS label as \"${BTRFS_LABEL_PREFIX}-${TARGET_LABELS[serial]}\", i.e. `das-backup-` + the config target label. That does not reproduce what is actually on the drives.

Measured 2026-08-31:

| config label | script would create | on disk today |
|---|---|---|
| primary-22tb | das-backup-primary-22tb | das-backup-22tb |
| system-recovery-A-2tb | das-backup-system-recovery-A-2tb | das-backup-system-recovery-A |
| system-recovery-B-2tb | das-backup-system-recovery-B-2tb | das-backup-system-recovery-B |

Re-partitioning any target therefore renames its filesystem. Impact is not yet established and needs its own verification cycle: backup-run.sh's bare-mountpoint guard verifies by filesystem UUID and device serial (not label), and mounts come from config.toml, so the immediate blast radius may be limited to btrbk.conf/documentation drift and to anything a human or script looks up by label. Establish that before choosing a fix.

Two candidate fixes: add an explicit per-target `fs_label` to config.toml, or derive the label so it round-trips against what is deployed. Whichever is chosen, add a pre-flight assertion that refuses to run when the label it is about to write differs from the label already on the target, so a re-partition cannot silently rename a filesystem other tooling depends on.

Found while correcting the ESP label defect in the same script (v2.1.0, 2026-08-31); deliberately NOT fixed there because the ESP change was provable in-session and this one is not.
close_reason:
FIXED in das-partition-drives.sh v2.2.0.

ROOT CAUSE: the BTRFS label was built as 'das-backup-' + the config TARGET ID, which reproduced no drive on disk. Re-partitioning any target silently RENAMED its filesystem.

FIX: the live label now wins. resolve_fs_label() reads the existing label off the target and preserves it verbatim; the derived name is a fallback for a genuinely blank drive only, and is reported as '(NEW — no existing filesystem found)' so the two cases are never confused. Re-partitioning destroys the data but must reproduce the same IDENTITY, or config.toml, btrbk.conf and every operator lookup stop resolving.

Deliberately NOT symmetric with the ESP label, and the asymmetry is the point: the deployed BTRFS labels are known-good and worth preserving, whereas the deployed ESP labels were historically a single shared 'BACKUP-ESP' across both recovery drives — a value we specifically do not want to perpetuate. Preserve a good identity; derive a corrected one. Both rationales are comments in the script.

Chose this over adding an fs_label field to config.toml: no schema change, no migration, and it cannot drift from what is deployed because it reads what is deployed.

VERIFIED END-TO-END against the live array — --check now plans exactly what blkid reports:
  /dev/sdj p2  das-backup-system-recovery-A  (preserved from disk)
  /dev/sdi p2  das-backup-system-recovery-B  (preserved from disk)
  /dev/sdl p1  das-backup-22tb               (preserved from disk)
Before the fix it planned das-backup-system-recovery-A-2tb, ...-B-2tb and das-backup-primary-22tb — none of which exist.

FALSIFIED: tests/test_esp_label_derivation.sh grew 7 cases for this (preserve, fallback, refuse-with-no-fallback, and partition selection 1 vs 2 asserted via a stubbed blkid), plus a structural check that every read_fs_label call site checks its status — that one was observed RED by deleting a '|| exit 1' and naming the exact line. Suite is 20/20.

title: Record a backup-throughput baseline and consume the Throughput Report
description:
backup-run.sh already emits "=== Throughput Report ===" (data written + MB/s per target,
see the script's own header note "Logs per-target throughput") every single run. Nothing
reads it, and nothing compares one run to the next. It is a producer with no consumer.

WHAT THAT COST (2026-08-19 to 2026-08-28):
The host's entire SuperSpeed USB tree went dark and every DAS bay silently dropped from
10 Gbit/s to 480 Mbit/s (~40 MB/s). The array ran nine days on a USB 2.0 link. Backups
still completed, just slower, and nothing flagged it:

  2026-08-26   1h 10m 37s
  2026-08-27   1h 05m 39s
  2026-08-28   1h 30m 09s     <- all of these at 480 Mbit/s

The link was restored to 10 Gbit/s on 2026-08-28 at ~19:00, so the FIRST RUN AT FULL
SPEED IS 2026-08-29 03:17. That run is the natural baseline datum -- capture it.

Note the ceiling will NOT scale with link rate: /etc/modprobe.d/terramaster-no-uas.conf
deliberately forces usb-storage (BOT) instead of UAS. BOT issues one command at a time
with no queuing, so above roughly Gen 1 the spindles and BOT are the limit, not the bus.
That quirk is a correct stability trade and should stay.

TASKS:
1. Record a throughput/duration baseline from the 2026-08-29 03:17 run, and the three
   480 Mbit/s runs above as the degraded reference.
2. Make the existing Throughput Report machine-readable enough to compare across runs
   (or emit a structured line alongside it).
3. Correct the docs that assert the enclosure is USB 3.2 Gen2 as though it were always
   true in practice -- docs/OFFLINE-BACKUP-PLAN.md and
   docs/examples/author-storage-reference.md both state it flatly. It was false for nine
   days and the docs could not have told anyone.
4. Add the safe re-cabling sequence to the operator docs: POWER THE ENCLOSURE DOWN before
   moving its cable. On 2026-08-28 15:03 the cable was pulled while udisks had all three
   backup filesystems mounted -> BTRFS emergency shutdown on all three, plus stale device
   registrations that REJECTED the returning disks ("duplicate device ... scanned by
   (udev-worker)") and left the array unmountable until cleared. No data was lost, but the
   array would have failed the unattended 03:17 run. Recovery procedure is written up in
   CachyOS-Kernel/docs/usb-topology.md section 8.

RELATED: detection of the link-speed regression itself is filed as cachyos-sentinel-unuc.
This issue is the backup-side consequence layer only.

/hddRaid1/ClaudeCodeProjects/CachyOS-Kernel/docs/usb-topology.md sections 5, 6, 8.
