title: job_cancel lets any authorized caller cancel any job — JobMap stores no owner
description:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-27 from ultrareview merged_bug_001, verified by reading the code.

btrdasd-helper.rs:63  type JobMap = Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, (JoinHandle<()>, CancelFlag)>>>  — no sender is stored, so ownership CANNOT be enforced even if the check wanted to.
btrdasd-helper.rs:1476 job_cancel: check_polkit(org.dasbackup.backup) then jobs.remove(job_id) + cancel + handle.abort(), unconditionally, for any id.
btrdasd-helper.rs:90   new_job_id() = format!('job-{ts}') from nanosecond SystemTime — enumerable, and ids are broadcast on JobProgress/JobLog/JobFinished to every bus subscriber.

The polkit action answers 'may this caller do backup operations', not 'does this caller own this job'.

SEVERITY CONTEXT: org.dasbackup.backup is auth_admin_keep (verified in the installed policy), so the threat model is a second authenticated admin, not any local user — a single-admin workstation is not practically exposed. Filed at P2 on that basis. Worth fixing because PR #42 priority 2 asked this exact question ('can a caller touch or cancel another client's job?') and the answer is yes.

IMPACT when it fires: handle.abort() drops MountGuard mid-operation, leaving partial restore data at the destination or a truncated btrbk send, with no error to the originating client — it just never sees JobFinished.
design: Store the sender bus name in JobMap at insert (every creator already has it from sender_from_header) and require it to match in job_cancel, returning AccessDenied on mismatch. Optionally add a random suffix to job ids.
acceptance_criteria: Client B cancelling client A's job is refused with AccessDenied — observed. Counter-test: A cancelling A's own job still succeeds.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.7.20.0. 388 unit tests + 2 root-gated loopback tests green; clippy clean; every new test observed RED against mutated code. Live-verified on the production host after deploy: wd7 (ConfigGet 0-arg works, old 1-arg form rejected 'Signature mismatch'), dca (lock free -> btrbk ran, 49 snapshots; lock genuinely held -> no btrbk process at all), s05 (/etc refused by denylist, /srv refused by allowlist, /tmp succeeded with correct content). 5ig verified by loopback falsification plus live confirmation of the naming premise: production btrbk wrote '.btrbk-snapshots/root-.20260828T0747', the hyphenated name the old hardcoded prefix could never match.

title: stream_command deadlocks if btrbk stderr exceeds the pipe buffer
description:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-27 from ultrareview bug_012. stream_command (indexer/src/backup.rs) reads stdout to EOF (for line in reader.lines()), THEN child.wait(), THEN drains stderr — verified by reading the function: stdout loop at relative line 18, wait() at 24, stderr taken at 35. Classic Unix pipe-buffer deadlock: once btrbk has written ~64 KiB (Linux default) to an undrained stderr pipe, its next write blocks in the kernel; blocked, it stops producing stdout; the parent blocks forever in reader.lines(); child.wait() is never reached.

run_command in the same file is NOT vulnerable — it uses Command::output(), which drains both streams concurrently.

BLAST RADIUS is what makes this worth fixing despite the trigger being uncommon: the deadlocked task holds the MountGuard and (once dca is fixed) the maintenance lock forever, so every subsequent backup AND the monthly scrub block until btrdasd-helper is kill -9'd. There is no timeout and no watchdog.

Callers: send_snapshots (btrbk resume) and run_full_pipeline (btrbk run).
design: Spawn a std::thread to drain stderr into a Vec<String> concurrently with the stdout loop; join it before/after child.wait(). Mirrors what Command::output() does internally.
acceptance_criteria: A child emitting >64 KiB of stderr completes instead of hanging — observed with a synthetic child. Counter-test: the same test hangs (times out) against the current ordering.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.7.20.0. 388 unit tests + 2 root-gated loopback tests green; clippy clean; every new test observed RED against mutated code. Live-verified on the production host after deploy: wd7 (ConfigGet 0-arg works, old 1-arg form rejected 'Signature mismatch'), dca (lock free -> btrbk ran, 49 snapshots; lock genuinely held -> no btrbk process at all), s05 (/etc refused by denylist, /srv refused by allowlist, /tmp succeeded with correct content). 5ig verified by loopback falsification plus live confirmation of the naming premise: production btrbk wrote '.btrbk-snapshots/root-.20260828T0747', the hyphenated name the old hardcoded prefix could never match.

title: Cross-ref: unmapped envelope sender noreply@localhost hard-bounces on the shared mail relay
description:
CROSS-REFERENCE ONLY — the defect lives in shared relay infrastructure owned by cachyos-sentinel (which owns /etc/postfix/sender_canonical and /usr/local/sbin/mail-relay-sync-credentials), not in DAS-Backup-Manager. Filed here because it was discovered during a DAS-Backup-Manager relay key-rotation verification on 2026-08-26 and would otherwise be dropped.

WHAT HAPPENS
Some local producer submits to the relay with envelope sender <noreply@localhost>. That address has no row in the relay's sender->credential map, so with smtp_sender_dependent_authentication=yes Postfix never attempts AUTH at all and Resend rejects at MAIL FROM:

  Aug 26 17:34:24 postfix/smtp: DD5B014FF3F6: relay=smtp.resend.com[54.205.195.44]:587,
    tls=secure, dsn=5.0.0, status=bounced (host smtp.resend.com said:
    530 Error: authentication Required (in reply to MAIL FROM command))

Seven such messages bounced in a single burst at 17:34:20-17:34:25 (sizes 1908-5020 bytes), each generating a null-sender bounce notification (14 log entries total). dsn=5.0.0 is a HARD bounce — those messages are permanently lost, not queued. No store-and-forward protection applies.

WHY IT IS NOT A KEY PROBLEM
530 at MAIL FROM means no credential row was found for the sender, so no AUTH was attempted. It is NOT 535 (invalid credentials). A key rotation neither causes nor fixes this.

ROOT CAUSE
/etc/postfix/sender_canonical rewrites only root, root@cachyos-bosco, bosco, and bosco@cachyos-bosco to sentinel@... . Nothing covers noreply@localhost, and the relay's SENDERS list has rows only for das-backup, sentinel, and library.

OPEN QUESTION — the producer is UNIDENTIFIED. The journal window around 17:34 shows only coincidental proton-bridge 503 noise. Identify it before choosing a fix.

WHY A FIX WAS NOT APPLIED
Adding noreply@localhost to the canonical map would rewrite an unknown producer's mail to the sentinel identity. .claude/rules/backup.md warns explicitly that a wrong envelope sender makes reports arrive under another project identity and selects another project key. The correct fix is to identify the producer, give it its own send-only Resend key and SENDERS row (the documented onboarding path), or fix it to submit with an already-mapped sender.

NOT AFFECTED: DAS-Backup-Manager itself. Its das-backup sender is mapped correctly and was verified end-to-end the same session (status=sent, 250 ca1f2bec-...).
acceptance_criteria: 1. The producer of noreply@localhost mail is identified by name. 2. It either gets its own send-only Resend key plus a SENDERS row, or is changed to submit with an already-mapped envelope sender. 3. A subsequent send from that producer reaches status=sent in journalctl -u postfix. 4. No 530 authentication-Required bounces appear for 7 days afterwards.
notes:
=== ATTRIBUTION INVESTIGATION 2026-08-26 22:35 CDT — concluded. Owner is Audiobook-Manager. ===

SUBMISSION PATH: all seven arrived via NETWORK SMTP to 127.0.0.1:25, not sendmail.
In the 17:34:00-17:35:00 window: postfix/pickup lines = 0, postfix/smtpd lines = 22.
Each was its own connection (ehlo=1 mail=1 rcpt=1 data=1 quit=1), client=localhost,
no sasl_method. That is an smtplib-shaped client, matching Audiobook-Manager's code.
Consequence: smtpd records no submitting uid or pid, so postfix cannot attribute it
(pickup would have logged uid=). Attribution had to come from host evidence.

HYPOTHESIS TESTED AND REFUTED — stale service environment.
audiobook-api.service carries EnvironmentFile=/etc/audiobooks/audiobooks.conf, which
is read only at unit start, so a config edit does not reach a running process. The
config was last edited 15:57:25. If the 17:34 instance had predated that, its
environment would have lacked SMTP_FROM and the fallback would follow.
It did not. All ten 'Started' events today: 09:56:34, 13:01:15, 13:03:55, 13:20:52,
15:08:55, 15:57:35, 17:09:03, 18:07:18, 21:11:50, 21:27:12. The instance live at
17:34 started 17:09:03 — 72 minutes AFTER the config edit — so it DID have
SMTP_FROM. (The current process confirms the mechanism works: SMTP_FROM/SMTP_HOST/
SMTP_PORT all present in /proc/<MainPID>/environ, checked as booleans.)
NOTE: the first pass at this list was truncated with head -20 and appeared to
support the hypothesis. The untruncated re-run refuted it. Do not truncate.

WHAT THAT LEAVES: no systemd unit logged ANY line in 17:34:15-17:34:30 (3 lines
total in the whole journal for that window, all unrelated proton-bridge 503 noise).
So the sender was a foreground / non-journald process — one of the four code paths
invoked OUTSIDE the systemd unit, where nothing exports SMTP_FROM: a shell, a test,
a cron entry without EnvironmentFile, or a script run by an interactive session.
The Audiobook-Manager session was actively verifying 9nu's mail paths at that
moment (9nu closed 17:10, commit 8ef153a8 at ~17:37), which is the only plausible
actor.

NOT DETERMINED — the exact invoking command. Evidence is exhausted, not merely
unexamined: smtpd logs no submitter identity; no unit logged; the bounce bodies
that would have carried the original headers are destroyed (see below); and that
session's ring buffer only reaches back to 21:44 CDT.

WHY THE BOUNCE BODIES ARE GONE — secondary finding, relay-side but NOT a defect:
relayhost is unconditional and 'localhost' is not in mydestination, so the seven
bounce notifications addressed to noreply@localhost were themselves shipped to
Resend and 530-bounced in turn. Double bounce, discarded. /var/spool/mail and
/var/mail are both empty. Total loss for the episode is 14 messages, not 7, and
the diagnostic evidence went with them. This is ordinary null-client behaviour
(empty mydestination), so it is recorded, not filed.

DISPOSITION: the fix is a code change in Audiobook-Manager, not a relay config
change. Audiobook-Manager-9nu was reopened tonight and now carries the full
mechanism and acceptance criteria. Recommend superseding this issue with 9nu
rather than filing a third.
close_reason:
SUPERSEDED BY Audiobook-Manager-9nu (reopened 2026-08-26 22:30 CDT).

bd supersede could not be used: it resolves the replacement id within the same
graph only, and 9nu lives in the Audiobook-Manager database. Cross-project
supersede is unsupported, so this is a close-with-reference instead — same
outcome, only available mechanism.

WHY IT MOVES: this was filed as a relay defect when the producer was unknown.
Investigation concluded the relay behaved CORRECTLY — it rejected mail from a
sender it holds no credential for, which is exactly what
smtp_sender_dependent_authentication exists to do. The defect is a code-level
fallback in Audiobook-Manager: four mail paths resolve the envelope sender as
os.environ.get("SMTP_FROM", "noreply@localhost"), and SMTP_FROM reaches the
process only via audiobook-api.service's EnvironmentFile. Invoked any other way,
they silently send under an identity the relay has no key for.

NOTHING IN RELAY CONFIG SHOULD CHANGE. In particular do NOT add noreply@localhost
to /etc/postfix/sender_canonical — rewriting it to another project's identity
would select that project's Resend key.

The full evidence chain lives in this issue's notes and is not duplicated in 9nu's:
submission-path forensics (pickup=0 vs smtpd=22, so no submitting uid is
recorded), the refuted stale-service-environment hypothesis with all ten restart
timestamps, the empty 15-second journal window, and why the bounce bodies that
would have named the sender no longer exist. Read this issue before re-opening
that line of investigation — the evidence is exhausted, not merely unexamined.

Fix and verification are tracked in Audiobook-Manager-9nu.

title: Full reindex degrades quadratically — 670 files/min at 4M rows makes btrdasd reindex --rebuild impractical
description:
A full rebuild of the production index is not completable. Measured 2026-08-25 on the live 22TB target: the first ~600k files indexed in ~6 minutes, then the rate collapsed to 670 files/min by 4.3M rows. Extrapolated to the full 16.8M-file index that is roughly 13 DAYS, against an estimate of hours. The run was stopped after 32 minutes at 204 of ~1300 snapshots and the index restored from backup.

CAUSE (confirmed by EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN, not inferred): indexer::index_snapshot pre-fetches the previous snapshot's entire file set via get_files_in_snapshot(prev_id) to build a HashMap for O(1) comparison. That query drives off 'SEARCH s USING INDEX idx_spans_last (last_snap>?)'. As snapshot ids climb, an ever-larger fraction of spans has last_snap >= the id being queried, so the scanned portion grows with the table and a back-to-back rebuild of ~1300 snapshots degrades quadratically. The process was CPU-bound (state R, ~51%) with a SQLite temp file open, not I/O-bound on USB.

NOT caused by the 5uq series scoping: the pre-5uq plan uses the SAME idx_spans_last driver and the added joins are two INTEGER PRIMARY KEY lookups per row — a constant factor. Both plans were captured side by side.

Why it never showed before: the index was built incrementally, a handful of snapshots per night against a table that grew slowly. Only a back-to-back rebuild concentrates the cost.

Consequence: btrdasd reindex --rebuild exists and is documented (0.7.14.0) but cannot be used on an index of this size, which also removes it as the repair route for opd and lc9. opd was instead fixed surgically (reconcile --repair). lc9's schema migration landed, but its DATA repair still needs a reindex, so lc9 cannot be completed until this is fixed.
design: Candidates, cheapest first: (a) index spans(first_snap, last_snap) or (last_snap, first_snap) so the containment predicate narrows on both ends instead of scanning a growing suffix; (b) have index_snapshot fetch the previous file set by SERIES rather than by id range, now that files carries a series column — a far smaller and better-indexed set; (c) build a rebuild-specific path that walks snapshots newest-first or batches inserts with indexes dropped and rebuilt at the end. (b) is likely the real fix and is now possible because of the lc9 schema change.
acceptance_criteria: A full rebuild of a 16.8M-file / 6500-snapshot index completes in a bounded, measured time (target: under a few hours) with the rate not collapsing as the table grows; the measurement is recorded.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-25 — the original '670 files/min, ~13 days' figure in this issue is WRONG and must not be quoted.

It was derived by sampling COUNT(*) FROM files a minute apart. Large snapshots are indexed inside a single transaction, so the visible row count sits perfectly flat while the work proceeds and then jumps by millions on commit. Sampling across such a window measures the transaction boundary, not throughput. The same run showed +1,625,996 in one 60s window and +0 in the next.

Valid comparison is elapsed time at matched snapshot counts, on the same target:
  161 snapshots — before 6:04, after ~3:16
  170 snapshots — before 18:32, after 14:31
  173 snapshots — before 21:13, after 16:31
  187 snapshots — before 24:29, after 17:31

So the series-scoped prev-fetch (0.7.18.0) is a genuine but MODEST improvement, roughly 1.3-1.9x, not the order of magnitude the bad figure implied. The quadratic term is reduced, not removed, which means the dominant cost is probably elsewhere — the filesystem walk over USB, or FTS/index maintenance on insert — and that has not been measured yet.

Requantify before doing further optimisation work: measure snapshots-per-elapsed-minute, or instrument index_snapshot directly, rather than polling row counts.
close_reason:
Fixed in 0.7.18.0 and MEASURED end-to-end 2026-08-25: a full 'btrdasd reindex --rebuild' of the production index completed in 40m53s (09:11:43 -> 09:52:36), exit 0, 610 of 610 snapshots and 8.9M files. Acceptance asked for a bounded, measured time under a few hours — met, and recorded here.

The fix: index_snapshot's prev-fetch now uses get_files_in_series_snapshot, so SQLite narrows on idx_files_series_path (series=?) instead of scanning a growing suffix of idx_spans_last (last_snap>=?). Only possible because files gained a series column in 0.7.14.0.

HONEST CAVEAT, kept deliberately: the original '670 files/min, ~13 days' figure in this issue was an artifact of polling COUNT(*) across transaction boundaries and is corrected in the notes. Measured properly at matched snapshot counts the improvement is ~1.3-1.9x, and at whole-job level roughly 3x (the abandoned pre-fix run reached 204 snapshots in 32 minutes; this one did 610 in 41). The quadratic term is reduced, not eliminated, and the dominant remaining cost — likely the USB filesystem walk or FTS maintenance on insert — has NOT been characterised. If rebuild time becomes a problem again, instrument index_snapshot directly rather than polling row counts.

title: files.path is UNIQUE and relative-within-snapshot — same path in two subvolumes shares one row
description:
files.path holds a path relative to the snapshot root (e.g. 'packaging/PKGBUILD', 'bosco/.cache/...') and carries a UNIQUE index. The same relative path occurring in two different source subvolumes therefore collapses into ONE files row, and upsert_file overwrites size/mtime with whichever subvolume was indexed last.

Measured on the production index 2026-08-24: 1,261,207 files have spans originating in more than one series.

Scope is narrower than it first appears, and specifically does NOT include presence: after 5uq, get_files_in_snapshot is scoped by the span's own series, and spans were verified series-coherent (0 of 85,038,167 incoherent), so each subvolume's listing is correct. What is wrong is file METADATA — size and mtime reported for a shared path belong to whichever subvolume upserted last, and btrdasd search shows that same conflated row.

Fixing it means keying files on (series, path) or adding a source discriminator, which is a schema migration plus a full reindex of 6515 snapshots — deliberately out of scope for the 0.7.13.0 release.
acceptance_criteria: Two subvolumes containing the same relative path with different size/mtime each report their own metadata via list and search; a regression test covers the collision; existing index migrated or rebuilt.
notes:
Schema half SHIPPED in 0.7.14.0/0.7.14.1: files is keyed on (series, path), upsert_file/get_file take the series, PRAGMA user_version tracks schema v2, and migrate() runs on open. Covered by tests including a genuine v1-database migration test.

DATA half still outstanding. The v1->v2 migration deliberately does not repair data — existing rows get series='' because the series of an already-collapsed row cannot be recovered — so only a re-index populates real values. That re-index is blocked by 3sa (quadratic rebuild). lc9 cannot be completed until 3sa is fixed; the schema is in place and ready for it.
close_reason:
COMPLETE 2026-08-25. Schema half shipped in 0.7.14.0/0.7.14.1 (files keyed on (series, path), upsert_file/get_file take the series, PRAGMA user_version + migrate()). DATA half completed by the full rebuild once 3sa made it feasible.

VERIFIED on the production index: 8,907,708 of 8,907,708 file rows carry a real series (zero left at ''), across 48 distinct series — one per configured subvolume, matching btrbk.conf's 48 snapshot_name entries. user_version=2, integrity ok, foreign_key_check zero rows.

Visible in output: 'btrdasd search PKGBUILD' now attributes packaging/PKGBUILD to ClaudeCodeProjects-claude-cowork-desktop-maintenance alone, where previously every project's PKGBUILD collapsed into a single row whose size/mtime were overwritten by whichever subvolume was indexed last.

title: btrdasd forget <pattern> — delete obsolete target snapshots and their index rows in one operation
description:
There is no command to remove obsolete snapshots from backups. The CLI surface (backup run/snapshot/send/boot-archive/report/record-run, subvol list/add/remove/set-manual/set-auto, restore file/snapshot/browse) has no delete/purge/prune verb. 'subvol remove' edits config to stop FUTURE backups; it does not touch existing ones.

The gap bites whenever a snapshot_name stops matching config — most commonly a project rename. Snapshots under the old name match no retention rule, so btrbk never prunes them: 'btrbk clean' handles incomplete/garbled only, 'btrbk prune' matches configured names. Deletion is manual btrfs subvolume delete across every target, with the index left stale afterward.

Worked example (2026-08-24): renaming ClaudeCodeProjects/claude-cowork-linux to -desktop-maintenance stranded 3 source + 21 target snapshots across 3 targets, requiring hand-written globs on each.

Proposed: 'btrdasd forget <glob>' resolves matching snapshots across all configured targets, shows a dry-run plan (count + reclaimed bytes per target), refuses any pattern that also matches a currently-configured snapshot_name, deletes with btrfs subvolume delete, and prunes the corresponding index rows.

Safety requirements, both non-negotiable:
  - NEVER clear ro on a received subvolume to edit content (backup.md: destroys Received UUID permanently, only btrfs receive can set it). Whole-snapshot deletion is the only safe granularity.
  - Must skip role=mirror targets' @/@home the way boot-archive-cleanup.sh does, so an independent recovery OS is never in scope.
design: Depends on index pruning (cu8) — deleting snapshots without reconciling the index just relocates the staleness. File-level deletion inside a received snapshot is deliberately out of scope and must stay that way.
acceptance_criteria: btrdasd forget --dry-run lists exactly the snapshots that would be deleted per target with reclaimed size; refuses patterns matching a live snapshot_name; deletes only via btrfs subvolume delete; index rows are pruned so search returns no hits in forgotten snapshots.
close_reason: Shipped in 0.7.16.0, VERIFIED live in both directions. The guard: 'btrdasd forget ClaudeCodeProjects-claude-cowork* --dry-run' refused with 'the pattern also matches ClaudeCodeProjects-claude-cowork-desktop-maintenance, a series btrbk is still backing up — narrow the pattern', naming the exact live chain it would otherwise have destroyed. The selection: the precise stranded pattern reported 'nothing matched', correctly, because by then the in-walk reconcile had already pruned those rows (cu8). Live series are read from /etc/btrbk/btrbk.conf, the file btrbk itself consumes, and the command exits rather than running unguarded if that file cannot be read. Eight unit tests cover the guard, selection, no-match and config parsing.

title: Migrate backup-report email from Protonmail Bridge to the Resend relay (das-backup@thebosco.club)
description:
Move all DAS backup-report email off Protonmail Bridge and onto the host's local
mail relay, sending as das-backup@thebosco.club via Resend.

WHY
Bridge is session-bound: its vault decrypts through KWallet, which only unlocks at a
real login. After an unattended reboot Bridge is down and every backup report is
silently lost — the same defect tracked as cachyos-sentinel-2q7b. The relay is a root
service with credentials under /etc and needs no session.

Design spec (read first, it is authoritative):
/hddRaid1/ClaudeCodeProjects/cachyos-sentinel/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-email-transport-design.md
Implementation plan for the relay itself:
/hddRaid1/ClaudeCodeProjects/cachyos-sentinel/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-03-local-mail-relay.md

DEPENDENCY — DO NOT START BEFORE THIS
The relay does not exist yet. Postfix is not installed, nothing listens on
127.0.0.1:25. Blocked on the cachyos-sentinel implementation (2q7b / 6m3s). Until it
lands, DAS keeps working on Bridge exactly as today; nothing breaks by waiting.
Verify before starting:  ss -ltn | grep ':25 '

CREDENTIAL — ALREADY EXISTS, DO NOT CREATE ANOTHER
A send-only Resend API key for this project already exists as RESEND_KEY_DAS_BACKUP
in ~/.config/api-keys.env (created 2026-08-03, verified send-only: GET /domains and
GET /api-keys both return 401 restricted_api_key).

DAS MUST NOT READ THAT KEY. It never touches a mail credential again. The key is
consumed only by /etc/postfix/sasl_passwd, generated by
/usr/local/sbin/mail-relay-sync-credentials, which already lists
das-backup@thebosco.club in its SENDERS table. Submission to the relay is
unauthenticated plaintext on loopback; Postfix authenticates upstream by envelope
sender.

Address creation is not required — thebosco.club is domain-verified at Resend, so
every address at the domain is a valid sender.

CHANGES

1. scripts/backup-run.sh
   - Delete parse_pbridge_smtp() entirely (lines ~1534-1578) and the PBRIDGE_CONF
     variable (~line 283) plus its comment block (~line 280). Leaving the parser
     behind is dead code.
   - Rewrite the mailx invocation (~lines 1602-1615):
       smtp=smtp://127.0.0.1:25
       -S smtp-auth=none
       drop -S smtp-auth-user, -S smtp-auth-password, -S ssl-verify=ignore
       -r "DAS Backup <das-backup@thebosco.club>"
   - Remove the 2>/dev/null on the mailx call. It currently discards the reason for
     every send failure; the log line says "Failed to email report" with no cause.
     The s-nail v14 deprecation noise it was hiding should be filtered specifically
     or tolerated, not used to justify swallowing real errors.

2. indexer/src/report.rs
   - Delete PbridgeSmtp (line 259), parse_pbridge_smtp_block() (line 273),
     PBRIDGE_CONF_DEFAULT (line 11), and percent_encode_userinfo() (line 242) —
     that helper exists only to encode credentials into the SMTP URL at lines
     443-444 and has no other consumer.
   - send_email_report_with_kind() (line 355) submits to 127.0.0.1:25 with no
     credentials and no TLS. The mailx child at line 451 keeps its args minus every
     auth setting.
   - From address becomes das-backup@thebosco.club.

3. indexer/src/config.rs
   - Default smtp_port 1025 -> 25 (line 698) and update the test asserting 1025
     (line 727).
   - EmailConfig.auth / AuthMethod (lines 424-430) becomes unreachable once
     submission is unauthenticated. Remove the field and the enum, or keep it only
     if some other consumer needs it — grep for consumers, not implementations,
     before deciding. A config key nothing reads is the zombie class this project
     has been burned by.
   - The deployed /etc/das-backup/config.toml carries smtp_host, smtp_port, from,
     to, auth under [email]. It is preserved across upgrades, so an upgraded host
     keeps smtp_port = 1025 and silently keeps talking to Bridge with new code. Ship
     a migration in the installer/upgrade path — do not rely on the compiled default.

SECURITY IMPROVEMENTS THIS DELIVERS (worth stating, they are not incidental)
- Both send paths currently put the SMTP password on a command line:
  backup-run.sh passes -S smtp-auth-password=..., and report.rs builds a
  smtp://user:pass@host URL for the mailx child. Either is readable in
  /proc/PID/cmdline by any local process for the lifetime of the send. After the
  migration DAS holds no credential at all, so the exposure disappears rather than
  being mitigated.
- ssl-verify=ignore goes away. It exists for Bridge's self-signed loopback cert;
  the relay hop is plain loopback, and the certificate-verified TLS leg to Resend
  is Postfix's job with smtp_tls_security_level = secure.

ACCEPTANCE
1. A real backup run emails a report that arrives at gjbr@pm.me IN THE INBOX, not
   spam, From das-backup@thebosco.club. A clean log is not acceptance.
2. Message headers show mailed-by send.thebosco.club and signed-by thebosco.club
   (SPF via the SES-covered subdomain, DKIM aligned to the From domain).
3. grep -rn 'pbridge\|PB_SMTP\|smtp-auth' scripts/ indexer/src/ returns nothing.
4. Stop postfix, run a backup, confirm the failure is logged with a cause and the
   report still lands in LAST_REPORT — the fallback must survive a down relay.
5. Reboot without logging in, trigger a backup, confirm the report arrives. This is
   the property Bridge could never provide and the whole reason for the work.

DO NOT
- Do not copy the Resend key into /etc/das-backup/config.toml, an env file, or any
  project config. One copy exists, in api-keys.env, and one derived artifact,
  /etc/postfix/sasl_passwd. Duplicated credential files drift silently — that is the
  documented pbridge.conf failure this replaces.
- Do not point automated mail at Proton SMTP submission "for tidiness". Apple

title: Manual btrdasd backup subcommands take no maintenance lock — outside the backup/scrub/doctor mutual-exclusion scheme
description: Found by 01u review 2026-08-02 (PLAUSIBLE, pre-existing). main.rs Commands::Backup handlers (Run/Snapshot/Send/BootArchive) call mount::ensure_sources_mounted/ensure_targets_mounted directly with NO /run/das-maintenance.lock acquisition — only scheduled backup-run.sh (bash flock), the scrub engine (scrub::acquire_locks), and now btrdasd doctor participate in the mutual-exclusion scheme. Concrete hazard: doctor (or a scrub/backup) mounts a source; a concurrent manual 'btrdasd backup run' sees it already mounted and uses it unregistered; doctor finishes first and unmounts it mid-use. Degrades gracefully in practice (umount EBUSY -> logged warning, non-destructive) but undercuts the documented mutual-exclusion guarantee. Fix: wire the manual Backup subcommand paths into the same two-lock pattern (own singleton? at minimum the shared maintenance lock, blocking with announce like the scheduled path). Audit BootArchive especially — it touches boot subvolumes. doctor.rs's module doc was scoped 2026-08-02 to stop claiming coverage it doesn't have (fix round of 01u).
close_reason: Fixed in 0.7.15.0, VERIFIED live: with /run/das-backup.lock held, 'btrdasd backup snapshot' printed 'A backup is already running — declining.' and did nothing. Run/Snapshot/Send/BootArchive now take the same singleton the scheduled path uses (so a manual run and the timer contend rather than running two backups over one target set) then the shared maintenance lock, in that order. Singleton non-blocking because a second backup is redundant rather than late; maintenance blocking because a scrub is a peer operation and the backup should wait. Also covered by unit tests against temp paths.

title: backup-run.sh ERR trap never fires for failures inside functions — cleanup()/unmount_all not guaranteed on set -e aborts (no errtrace)
description: Flagged during ecg round-2 fix 2026-08-02, empirically reproduced on bash 5.3.15: scripts/backup-run.sh uses 'set -euo pipefail' WITHOUT -E/-o errtrace, and 'trap cleanup ERR' is set inside main(). Under this combination the ERR trap fires only for a failing command directly in main()'s own body — never for failures inside called functions (mount_targets, run_btrbk, verify_targets_before_btrbk, etc.). Consequence: any set -e abort or explicit exit 1 inside a function skips cleanup() entirely — no unmount_all, no FAILURE DB row, DAS left mounted, run vanishes from history. Pre-existing systemic property, NOT introduced by the v4.4.0 ecg change (whose new call sites are individually guarded with || true). Candidate fixes when picked up: (a) set -E + trap ... ERR at top level (test interaction with intentional nonzero returns like flock probes and grep -c idioms — errtrace changes semantics broadly, needs a careful audit of every 'harmless nonzero' site); (b) trap cleanup EXIT with a success flag (fires on ANY exit path incl. exit 1 in functions — likely the safer pattern); (c) leave architecture, document the invariant that any function-level abort must do its own unmount. Reproductions: false / exit 1 / x=$(false) inside a function all killed the script with zero cleanup() output. Related: the ecg review's Finding 2 analysis (2026-08-02) has the full trace.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-08-02 in 81aa292 (backup-run.sh v4.4.1). trap cleanup ERR (never fired inside functions — no errtrace; reproduced on bash 5.3.15) replaced with top-level EXIT trap + two gates: SCRIPT_COMPLETED (clean-completion no-op) and CLEANUP_ARMED (recovery body only after acquire_maintenance_lock() — pre-ownership aborts like usage errors/check_root must NOT unmount_all over /mnt/backup-* that a concurrent scrub may hold under the same lock). INT/TERM route through EXIT with explicit 130/143 (bare 'trap exit' proven to reuse stale $? — systemctl stop would have reported 0). rc captured first, exited explicitly — unmount results can't mask abort codes. PROOF: 10-case harness on extracted real code (function-depth exit 1/abort 42 recover with codes preserved; clean real/dryrun no-op exit 0; TERM/INT 143/130; recursion fires once; pre-arm usage-error/early-exit skip recovery with codes preserved) + real flock-held second-instance defer (exit 0, no mounts touched) + real --dryrun end-to-end exit 0 + md5 byte-identity installed-vs-repo. Note: orchestrator's initial singleton-skip disaster scenario was DISPROVEN by the implementer (top-of-file flock exit predates trap install); the real exposure was the post-trap pre-maintenance-lock window, fixed via the arming gate. shellcheck/bash -n clean.

title: Sentinel × das-scrub.service failure-retry loop — persistent scrub failure triggers indefinite multi-hour repasses
description: Final-review finding 2026-08-01. btrdasd scrub run exits 1 when any FS fails -> das-scrub.service enters failed -> sentinel-core auto-restarts failed units (no exclusion for das-scrub in /etc/sentinel/, verified). A PERSISTENT scrub failure (exactly the case where scrub finds real damage, e.g. uncorrectable errors on the single-device 2TB drives) = each Sentinel retry is another multi-hour full pass: indefinite scrub-looping on a failing drive, FAILURE email per pass, backups deferred behind each pass via the maintenance lock. Options: (a) Sentinel exclusion for das-scrub.service in /etc/sentinel/ config; (b) exit-0-with-alerting semantics — arguably correct since health already escalates scrub failure to Critical and the email already says FAILURE, so exit-1 is a redundant alarm channel that only exists to feed the wrong consumer. Decide + implement BEFORE first scheduled fire 2026-09-01 05:30.
notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-02 08:35 (cross-check of the sentinel repo): Sentinel made NO code change — their bd records (cachyos-sentinel-xb18/b4x1, open) say NO SENTINEL CHANGE REQUIRED; the agreed fix is DAS-SIDE exit-code semantics. Their restart path is unchanged (RestartTracker 3/600s, exact-match never_touch, no policy gate — ivrf still open). title: [scrub 2/6] Scrub engine: indexer/src/scrub.rs — sequential per-FS scrub with mount-by-UUID, finished-vs-aborted, maintenance lock
description:
New module indexer/src/scrub.rs. Runs the monthly pass: for each configured target IN SEQUENCE — mount by FS UUID (targets are unmounted between backups; cannot rely on any backup mount window), btrfs scrub start + wait, parse the persistent record /var/lib/btrfs/scrub.status.<fsuuid>, unmount when done.

HARD REQUIREMENTS (both from the 2026-07-27 recovery-A investigation):
1. MUST distinguish finished from aborted. The 2026-05-24 record read 'Status: aborted, super=3, Total to scrub: 0.00B' and was silently treated as fine for 64 days. aborted OR any nonzero error counter = failure result for that FS.
2. MUST resolve everything by FS UUID, never mount path. 'btrfs scrub status <path>' after an unmount silently returns the record of whatever FS backs the path (observed: NVMe root's record) — same hazard class as bd 9on.

LOCKING (two-lock design, checkpoint-notes 18:05):
- Own singleton: flock -n on /run/das-scrub.lock — skip if a scrub is already running.
- Then BLOCKING flock on /run/das-maintenance.lock (shared with backup-run.sh, task b6f) held for the entire pass incl. its own mounts/unmounts. This is the mutual-hold interlock: deferral, never cancellation, auto-release on process exit/death. Log when the wait is non-trivial.
- Locks acquired singleton→maintenance on both sides (no deadlock). /run is tmpfs (no stale locks).

RESULTS: per-FS outcome (finished/aborted/errors, byte counts, duration) persisted for task 5kb (health) and emailed via the existing send_report/pbridge.conf pipeline (user decision: existing email path; send on completion or abort with any error).

Unbounded: no time box, no RuntimeMaxSec — an overrun simply defers the next backup on the lock.

title: btrdasd-helper IndexStats/Index* methods block async runtime, GUI hits 25s D-Bus timeout on cold cache
description:
Symptom (2026-05-24 ~08:30 CDT, user-reported): ButteredDASD GUI Health Dashboard showed dialog 'IndexStats: Did not receive a reply. Possible causes include: ... the reply timeout expired'. Status bar showed 'DB: 0 B | 0 snapshots' as the GUI's fallback display when IndexStats returns nothing.

Verified the helper is healthy (218 ms warm IndexStats via gdbus). Data is intact (10.1 GB DB, 13.7M files, 1707 snapshots, 68M spans). The dialog was a transient timeout, not a real failure.

Root cause (two-fault):
1. ARCHITECTURAL: indexer/src/bin/btrdasd-helper.rs index_stats, index_list_snapshots, index_list_files, index_search, index_backup_history, index_snapshot_path were 'async fn' but did blocking SQLite I/O directly on the runtime worker thread instead of tokio::task::spawn_blocking. The backup_run / backup_snapshot / health_query methods all correctly use spawn_blocking. Under memory pressure, blocking the runtime thread can serialize subsequent calls until the worker drains.
2. COLD-CACHE AMPLIFICATION: 10 GB SQLite on HDD takes ~4 s cold (after drop_caches) vs 91 ms warm. Overnight idle = kernel evicts DB pages = morning GUI hits the cold path. Combined with #1, a cold IndexStats can exceed the GUI's 25 s D-Bus call timeout.

Fix: wrap all 6 index_* read methods in tokio::task::spawn_blocking (mirroring health_query's pattern), and add mmap_size=4GiB + cache_size=-262144 (256 MiB) PRAGMAs to Database::open so cold-cache reads use kernel mmap rather than per-call sqlite read syscalls.

Acceptance: gdbus IndexStats call returns in <500 ms cold (after drop_caches) and <250 ms warm. GUI Health Dashboard opens without IndexStats timeout dialog under normal use.

On a cache hit, IndexStats does a cheap fs::metadata then returns instantly from RAM — verified to serve from cache even after 'echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'. Cache only invalidates when the indexer bumps the DB mtime (which means exactly: after each indexer run).

title: Build subvolume drift detector — catch unbacked-up subvolumes before they become silent gaps
description:
Today's audit (2026-05-17, follow-up to bd 15i) revealed that ~30 subvolumes across 3 filesystems were never being backed up — including all 22 nested ClaudeCodeProjects/* (= ALL user code), audiobook app state (database + config + var-lib), @hibp, @docker, bosco-media, ISOs, SteamLibrary, SteamLibrary-local. The gap accumulated silently over months as subvolumes were added (for new projects, for new apps like Audiobook-Manager, for the Steam migration) without corresponding config.toml updates. Existing backups were running successfully every day, masking the omission.

The fix is a 'drift detector' subcommand:
  btrdasd doctor --check-drift
    or
  btrdasd audit subvolumes

Algorithm:
1. For each [[source]] in config.toml, take the volume (e.g. /.btrfs-nvme).
2. Mount it if not mounted (the script's normal volume mount logic).
3. Run btrfs subvolume list, get every top-level + nested subvolume on the FS.
4. Apply built-in exclusion patterns:
   - .snapshots/* (Snapper-managed)
   - .btrbk-snapshots/* (btrbk's own)
   - @tmp, @var-tmp (ephemeral)
   - Any user-configurable additional patterns
5. Compare the filtered subvolume list against the union of every [[source]].subvolume name in config.toml.
6. Report subvolumes found on disk but NOT in config — these are silent omissions.
7. Optionally report the inverse — config entries with no matching subvolume (stale config).
8. Exit non-zero if any drift detected, so a systemd timer can auto-warn via email.

UX considerations:
- Output should categorize: 'definitely should add' (irreplaceable: code, DB, configs) vs 'probably skip' (rebuildable: caches, build artifacts).
- Output should suggest a config.toml diff that would close the gap.
- Run as a weekly systemd timer (e.g., das-backup-doctor.timer Sunday 02:00, before the backup window), with email-on-drift.

Companion: backup-run.sh should ALSO surface per-source skip warnings in the email report (covered by bd 0p2). The drift detector is the proactive check; bd 0p2 is the in-band surfacing.

Acceptance: btrdasd doctor (or similar) detects all 4 HDD media subvolumes if they weren't in config; detects the 22 ClaudeCodeProjects/* if they weren't in config; ignores .snapshots and .btrbk-snapshots paths; exit code 1 on drift detected.

title: backup-run.sh: auto-create snapshot_dir for sources, silently skipping is a footgun
description:
Discovered 2026-05-17 during full subvolume audit (DAS-Backup-Manager-15i follow-up work). When config.toml has a [[source]] with snapshot_dir = X that doesn't exist on disk yet (because the source is newly added), btrbk silently warns and SKIPS the entire source. backup-run.sh records the partial-failure as btrbk exit code 10 but the SPECIFIC SOURCES THAT WERE SKIPPED are not visible in the email report or DB — only the generic 'btrbk: exit code 10' marker.

Symptom seen 2026-05-17 run 125: added hdd-media (bosco-media, SteamLibrary) and hdd-system (ISOs, SteamLibrary-local) sources with snapshot_dir = '.btrbk-snapshots' (resolving to /.btrfs-hdd/.btrbk-snapshots). That dir didn't exist on the HDD top-level. btrbk emitted 'WARNING: Skipping subvolume X: Failed to fetch subvolume detail for snapshot_dir' lines (only visible in journal, not surfaced in script summary). All 4 subvolumes silently skipped. Run marked 'Failed' with btrbk exit 10 but no per-subvol indication of WHICH.

Fix needed: in backup-run.sh, in the 'Creating btrbk snapshot directories' block (which currently iterates known dirs), enumerate config.toml's [[source]].snapshot_dir values and mkdir -p each one on its respective volume BEFORE invoking btrbk. Probably already partially does this — see scripts/backup-run.sh 'Creating btrbk snapshot directories...' line and surrounding logic, may have a gap for newly-added sources.

Additional defense: parse btrbk's WARNING lines in the report-generation code and surface them in the email report + DB errors column. Right now the WARNING messages live only in the journal and aren't visible without active diagnosis.

This is part of the broader 'config drift detector' work — backup-run.sh should fail-loudly when its sources aren't being backed up as expected, not silently skip them and continue.

Pre-existing snapshot dirs in older volumes had been hand-created at some point and masked the bug — every "working" snapshot dir on disk was a coincidence, not a result of the script's logic.

Fix (commit 30ed7db, v4.2.2→v4.2.3): create_snapshot_dirs now composes ${SOURCE_VOLUMES[label]}/${SOURCE_SNAPSHOT_DIRS[label]} when the snapshot_dir is relative, respects absolute paths as-is, warns and skips on unknown source volume, logs each resolved path, and surfaces mkdir failures. title: GUI: collapse 6-dialog startup cascade into single 'helper unavailable' error
description:

title: Add install-time zero-byte binary validation to CMakeLists.txt
description: Defense-in-depth follow-up to DAS-Backup-Manager-29j. The May 10 install pass produced three 0-byte stubs (backup-run.sh, btrdasd, btrdasd-helper) because cmake install(PROGRAMS \"\${CARGO_TARGET_DIR}/release/...\") faithfully copies whatever is at the source path, even if 0 bytes. Add an install(CODE ...) block at the end of CMakeLists.txt that runs file(SIZE) on every installed Rust binary and FATAL_ERRORs if any are zero. This catches the bug at install time instead of at runtime (when the user gets a startup-job-failed dialog). Belongs in this project's CMakeLists.txt, not in a separate script (single-canonical-source rule).

- Hypothesis: someone may have run a bare 'install' or 'cp' command from outside cmake's normal flow, OR a previous cmake --install ran when build/cargo-target had a 0-byte stub (briefly, mid-cargo-rebuild).
- Cargo registry corruption (/home/bosco/.cargo/registry/src/ had 689 zero-byte files from a different incident, cleared during this session) suggests the host has had a pattern of file-truncation events possibly related to BTRFS snapshot operations or system interruptions during writes.

The defense-in-depth in 9rx (das_require_nonzero_artifact pre-checks before each Rust install rule) now catches this bug class at install time with a FATAL_ERROR and a clear message — so if the underlying defect recurs, the user/operator will see exact, real-time evidence (which install command, which artifact, what state of the build tree) that this retrospective investigation lacked. title: Fail-silent cluster in the reviewed files: btrbk counter grep, MountGuard::Drop, mkdir shell-outs, schedule parsers
description:

title: Recovery targets are never indexed — snapshot dedup keys on (source, name, ts), not target
description:
Observed during the 2026-08-25 full rebuild:

  primary-22tb:          610 indexed of 610 on disk
  system-recovery-B-2tb:   0 indexed of 237 on disk
  system-recovery-A-2tb:   0 indexed of 237 on disk

Working as designed, not a regression. discover_snapshots dedups on (source, name, ts) with the explicit comment 'the same snapshot may appear under different mount paths (bind mount vs udisks2)'. A snapshot replicated to all three targets is the same logical snapshot, so it is indexed once — under whichever target is walked first, always the primary.

Consequence worth deciding on: every indexed path points at /mnt/backup-22tb. If the 22TB array is unavailable and the operator needs to restore from a recovery drive, search and list can tell them WHICH snapshot holds a file but not that a copy exists on the mounted recovery target — the path they get names a filesystem that is not there. Nothing is lost (the data is on the recovery drive either way) but the index cannot help locate it.

Also explains why the retired /mnt/backup-system-mirror and /mnt/backup-system rows existed at all: those paths were the primary at the time.

Not urgent — the recovery drives are for a disaster in which the operator is working by hand anyway. Recording it because 'the index only ever describes one target' is a real property that is nowhere written down, and the 0-of-237 line looks like a bug to anyone who has not read discover_snapshots.
acceptance_criteria: Either the index records per-target presence (e.g. a snapshot_targets table) so restore can name a reachable copy, or the single-target behaviour is documented in ARCHITECTURE.md and the reindex summary stops printing '0 indexed of 237' without explanation.
close_reason:
Resolved in 0.7.19.0 by the FIRST acceptance option — the index now records per-target presence — which also subsumes the second (the misleading summary line is gone).

New snapshot_targets(snapshot_id, target_root, path) table, schema v3, with ON DELETE CASCADE so presence rows cannot outlive their snapshot and reintroduce the stale-row problem cu8 was about (asserted by a test). walk records presence for newly-indexed snapshots and for copies already indexed from another target; an existing copy's files are deliberately not re-read, since it is the same logical snapshot.

VERIFIED live 2026-08-25 after 'btrdasd reindex':
  /mnt/backup-22tb                610 copies
  /mnt/backup-system-recovery-A   237 copies
  /mnt/backup-system-recovery-B   237 copies
  1084 presence rows total; user_version 3, integrity ok, foreign_key_check 0 rows.

The summary now reads '237 copies recorded of 237 on disk (already indexed from another target)' instead of a bare '0 indexed of 237 on disk', which read as a failure while being correct behaviour. --json gains copies_recorded per target.

Recording it immediately surfaced a fact that was previously unknowable: 373 of 610 snapshots exist ONLY on the primary. If the 22TB array were lost, those are gone and 237 survive on the recovery drives — exactly the question the index could not answer before.

Presence had to be stored rather than derived: the recovery targets keep daily=7 only against the primary's daily/weekly/monthly/yearly, so they hold a subset (295 snapshot directories against 730).

title: Index rows under retired mount paths can never be reconciled — 92 immortal rows
description:
reconcile only nominates a snapshot for pruning when its path sits under a target root that is currently a VERIFIED MOUNTPOINT. That guard is correct and load-bearing. But it means rows whose root no longer appears in config.toml at all are unreachable forever: the root will never be mounted again, so the pass can never confirm the path is gone, so the rows are skipped on every run.

Measured on the production index after the 0.7.13.1 deploy: 92 such rows, under two roots retired by the 2026-05-17 rename:
  /mnt/backup-system-mirror/  — 44 rows
  /mnt/backup-system/         — 48 rows
Current config targets are /mnt/backup-22tb, /mnt/backup-system-recovery-A, /mnt/backup-system-recovery-B, so neither retired root resolves.

These rows are inert rather than harmful — nothing lists or restores from a path that cannot be mounted — but they will accumulate on every future target rename, and 'Skipped (unmounted)' in the reconcile summary conflates them with the genuinely-transient case (a target that simply is not mounted right now), so the count never goes to zero and stops being a signal.

Deliberately NOT fixed by relaxing the mountpoint guard, which exists to stop an unmounted target from wiping the whole index.
design: Reporting split first: ReconcilePlan folded 'unknown root' into skipped_unmounted precisely because it could not tell them apart with only mounted roots passed in. Passing the full configured-root list alongside the mounted subset restores the distinction without weakening the guard.
acceptance_criteria: Rows under roots absent from config are distinguishable from rows under a configured-but-currently-unmounted root; an explicit, separately-confirmed path exists to retire them (e.g. 'btrdasd reconcile --forget-root <path>'); the production 92 are cleared.
close_reason: Shipped in 0.7.16.0 (reporting split) and 0.7.17.0 (--forget-root), VERIFIED live and the production rows CLEARED. reconcile now reports 'Skipped (retired root): 92 — under a mount path no longer in config' separately from the transient unmounted count, which previously masked it. reconcile --forget-root then dropped them explicitly: 44 rows under /mnt/backup-system-mirror and 48 under /mnt/backup-system, both retired by the 2026-05-17 rename. The guard was proven too — --forget-root /mnt/backup-22tb refused with 'IS a configured target ... dropping its rows would discard a live index'. Final state: 0 retired-root rows; reconcile --dry-run reports Confirmed present 610, Skipped 0, Stale 0. Prefix matching is anchored on a path boundary so /mnt/backup-22 cannot capture /mnt/backup-22tb, asserted in both directions.

title: Three surviving mutants in db.rs — untested PRAGMA sign, usage-history window, and Drop
description:
cargo-mutants (27.1.0) over indexer/src/db.rs and indexer/src/reconcile.rs: 206 mutants, 164 unviable, 39 caught, 3 missed. All three survivors are pre-existing and unrelated to 5uq/cu8; the 11 misses that existed in or adjacent to that work were closed during the 0.7.13.0 release.

Survivors:
  - db.rs:141:48  'delete -' in Database::open — cache_size is set to -262144, where the SIGN selects the unit (negative = KiB, positive = pages). Dropping it silently changes the cache from 256 MiB to 262144 pages (~1 GiB at 4K). Performance-only, but nothing asserts it.
  - db.rs:663:13  'replace - with /' in get_target_usage_history — the cutoff is now_secs - (days * 86400). A mutated operator changes which rows the history window returns and no test notices.
  - db.rs:723:9   'replace Drop::drop with ()' — the impl runs 'PRAGMA optimize' on close. Hard to assert behaviourally; may warrant a deliberate #[mutants::skip] with a comment rather than a test.

Reproduce: cd indexer && cargo mutants --in-place --file src/db.rs --file src/reconcile.rs --timeout 120 -- --lib
NOTE: --in-place is REQUIRED. Without it cargo-mutants copies only the crate dir, setup/templates.rs include_str!("../../../scripts/*.sh") fails to resolve, and the run exits 0 having tested NOTHING ('cargo build failed in an unmutated tree, so no mutants were tested').
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three is either covered by a test that fails when the mutant is applied, or carries an explicit #[mutants::skip] with a documented reason; a clean run reports 0 missed.
notes:
Line numbers drift with edits — locate by function name, not line. As of v0.7.13.2 the three survivors are Database::open (cache_size sign), Database::get_target_usage_history (history-window subtraction), and the Drop impl.

Reproduce: cd indexer && cargo mutants --in-place --file src/db.rs --file src/reconcile.rs --timeout 120 -- --lib
--in-place is REQUIRED. Without it cargo-mutants copies only the crate dir, setup/templates.rs include_str!("../../../scripts/*.sh") fails to resolve, and the run exits 0 having tested NOTHING ('cargo build failed in an unmutated tree, so no mutants were tested').

Trend across the 0.7.13.x work: 14 missed / 28 caught -> 3 missed / 43 caught.
close_reason: Shipped in 0.7.15.0/0.7.16.0. cache_size's sign (KiB vs pages) and get_target_usage_history's cutoff arithmetic are now covered, as is the newly added series_key. VERIFIED: cargo mutants --in-place over db.rs and reconcile.rs reports 226 mutants, 52 caught, 174 unviable, 0 MISSED. The one genuinely untestable mutant (Drop::drop, which issues PRAGMA optimize and exposes no observable result) is excluded in indexer/.cargo/mutants.toml with its reason recorded, along with a note that --in-place is mandatory in this crate or the run exits 0 having tested nothing.

title: backup_runs.snaps_created/snaps_sent stuck at 0 since 2026-06-26 — btrbk 'up-to-date' counting broken (pre-existing, not the ecg reorder)
description: Found during ecg real-run proof 2026-08-02. record_backup_run_in_db() derives snaps_created via grep -c 'up-to-date' on btrbk list latest output; DB shows the counting worked through run id 173 (2026-06-25, values like 97/97) and has been 0/0 on EVERY run since id 174 (2026-06-26) — including 2026-08-02 03:34/04:28 runs on v4.3.1 which still called btrbk live pre-unmount, so this is NOT caused by the ecg cache reorder (which preserved the counting semantics exactly, per brief). Likely cause: btrbk upgrade around 2026-06-25/26 changed list-latest output (STATUS column now shows '-'; 'up-to-date' string gone — verify btrbk version/pacman log for that date and the current output format). Effect: GUI backup-history shows 0 snapshots created/sent for every run for 5+ weeks — a silent-zombie stat. Fix: re-derive counts from the actual btrbk output format (e.g. count '+++ ' created-snapshot lines and '>>>' received lines from the run log, or btrbk list latest column parsing by position), add a regression check that a real run records nonzero counts when snapshots were demonstrably created. bytes_sent/duration are unaffected and correct.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.7.15.0, VERIFIED live on the 2026-08-25 scheduled run: backup_runs id 244 recorded snaps_created=48, snaps_sent=126 — nonzero and genuinely distinct — against 0|0 on every run since id 174 (2026-06-26). Root cause confirmed rather than assumed: btrbk 0.32.7 renders the STATUS column as '-' for every row and the string 'up-to-date' the counters grepped for appears zero times in its output, measured directly. Counts now derive from btrbk --format=raw, whose named key='value' fields are an interface rather than a table layout, and snaps_sent is no longer a proxy for snaps_created (one subvolume yields one snapshot replicated to N targets).

title: setup --upgrade never prunes files dropped from the regenerated manifest — stale installed files linger
description: Confirmed by myq review 2026-08-02: installer.rs upgrade() -> install() -> install_to_prefix() builds manifest_entries fresh from GeneratedFiles::generate() and unconditionally overwrites /etc/das-backup/.manifest without diffing against the prior manifest, so files that drop out of the generated set are never deleted from disk. Concrete instance: the myq migration left the orphaned /usr/lib/das-backup/scripts/ symlink dir on disk (removed by hand after a reference-free grep proof). Mitigating: uninstall_all()'s remove_dir_all on {prefix}/lib/das-backup would sweep such orphans, but plain uninstall() is manifest-driven only, and any future file-shape change (renamed unit, dropped script) re-creates the exposure. Fix: in upgrade(), read the prior manifest before overwriting; for each path present in old but absent in new, remove the file (with the same safety posture as uninstall — never remove paths outside the known prefixes/etc locations); log each pruned path. Add unit test simulating a shape change across two install_to_prefix calls.
close_reason: Shipped in 0.7.15.0. install_to_prefix() now reads the prior manifest before overwriting it and removes paths absent from the newly generated set, logging each; the config file is never pruned. VERIFIED by two tests the issue asked for — a shape change across two install_to_prefix calls removes the dropped file and its manifest entry, and the config survives a re-install.

title: setup --upgrade can silently revert canonical scripts when btrdasd binary is stale (include_str! two-writer hazard)
description: Flagged by myq review 2026-08-02 (PLAUSIBLE, pre-existing — myq made the write path direct instead of via the 2026-05-23 symlink accident, net exposure equal). Scenario: developer edits scripts/backup-run.sh, runs cmake --install (flat file updated), but installed btrdasd was built BEFORE the edit. Next 'sudo btrdasd setup --upgrade' writes the STALE include_str!-embedded SCRIPT_BACKUP_RUN over the just-updated canonical /usr/lib/das-backup/backup-run.sh — silent downgrade, no warning. setup --upgrade's own docstring encourages re-running it freely, so this is a real footgun. Candidate fixes: embed a content hash/build stamp and warn (or refuse without --force) when the on-disk script differs from the embedded copy AND the binary mtime is older than the on-disk file; or have upgrade skip script installation when cmake's copy is newer; or drop script installation from setup entirely (cmake being the sole script writer — cleanest single-writer answer, but breaks non-cmake installs if any exist). Session workflow already mitigates in practice (cmake --install always follows builds here).
close_reason: Shipped in 0.7.15.0. An on-disk file NEWER than the running binary is no longer overwritten by the include_str! copy, with a line explaining why; the normal direction still writes, because after a rebuild the binary is newer than the file. VERIFIED by a matched pair of tests: a script stamped into the future survives an upgrade byte-for-byte, and one stamped into the past is refreshed — the second guarding against implementing 'keep newer' as 'never write', which would silently stop upgrades working.

title: report.rs format_report() drifts from backup-run.sh generate_report() — Rust manual-path report lacks Archive cleanup and Unmount rows
description: Found by ecg review 2026-08-02. indexer/src/report.rs format_report() (used by the Rust/manual 'btrdasd backup run' path) builds its own BACKUP OPERATIONS section whose doc comment (report.rs:27) claims it matches the shell script's format — but it predates and lacks the 'Archive cleanup' row (pre-existing drift) and now also lacks the 'Unmount targets' row added to scripts/backup-run.sh v4.4.0 (bd ecg). No programmatic consumer parses either report's text (verified by grep during the ecg review — nothing reads LAST_REPORT or matches these section strings), so this is cosmetic/consistency drift, not breakage. Options when picked up: (a) port the missing rows to format_report() with whatever unmount/cleanup status the Rust path actually tracks (MountGuard has its own unmount handling — the row must reflect Rust-path reality, not fake parity); (b) or update the report.rs:27 comment to stop claiming format parity and document the intentional divergence. Decide based on whether the Rust manual path even performs archive cleanup (it calls archive_boot, not boot-archive-cleanup.sh) — parity may be actively misleading.
close_reason: Shipped in 0.7.15.0, resolved as option (b) from the issue. Porting the missing rows would have been worse than the drift: the shell path's 'Archive cleanup' row reports boot-archive-cleanup.sh, which the Rust path does not run (it calls archive_boot and nothing prunes after), and its 'Unmount targets' row reports the script's own unmount_all where the Rust path delegates to MountGuard. Emitting them would report work that did not happen. The doc comment now documents the divergence instead of denying it. VERIFIED: grep across the tree confirms nothing parses either report's text — only the generator and its own test reference the section strings, and DAS_LAST_REPORT is a path export, not a parser.

title: backup-run.sh: unmount FAIL result never reaches the same-run email report
description:
Discovered 2026-08-01 while implementing bd b6f. unmount_all() now honestly
tracks DAS target unmount failures via record_op("unmount", ...), and the
final "safely disconnected" console/journal message is correctly gated on
it. But in main()'s real (non-dryrun) path, generate_report()/send_report()
run BEFORE unmount_all() -- the report needs targets still mounted for
DISK CAPACITY / GROWTH ANALYSIS (df-based). So OP_STATUS[unmount] is set
after the email has already gone out; a target that fails to unmount this
run will show up in the journal and console (and the next run's
verify_targets_before_btrbk gate) but not in this run's own email.

Fixing properly would mean either caching capacity/growth data before the
unmount (restructuring capture_usage/generate_capacity_section /
generate_growth_section to use cached values instead of a live df) or
sending a small follow-up notification specifically for a post-report
unmount failure. Out of scope for b6f (which only asked for OP_STATUS +
suppressing the disconnect claim, both of which work correctly and are
harness-verified). Tracked here so the gap isn't silently lost.
notes: Implementation committed 38c5b0a 2026-08-02 (v4.4.0, cache-then-reorder + Unmount row + 2 review-round fixes: cached BTRBK_LATEST feeds record_backup_run_in_db counts; df guards in capture_report_data). Reviewed adversarially (2 criticals found+fixed+harness-proven). REMAINING before close: real-run proof — one systemd das-backup run must show the Unmount targets row in the delivered email (session Step 6). Spawned issues: 39w (report.rs drift), oeo (ERR-trap gap).
close_reason: Fixed in 38c5b0a (backup-run.sh v4.4.0, cache-then-reorder + Unmount targets row; hardened in 81aa292 v4.4.1). REAL-RUN PROOF 2026-08-02 16:05-17:07 (systemd das-backup.service, Result=success, exit 0, zero warnings in window): journal + /var/lib/das-backup/last-report.txt (the exact emailed bytes) show 'All volumes unmounted' 17:07:08 THEN report generation 17:07:09 with 'Unmount targets OK (all clean)' row in BACKUP OPERATIONS, Status ALL OPERATIONS SUCCESSFUL, 'Report emailed to gjbr@pm.me' (SMTP accepted 17:07:13) — the unmount result now demonstrably reaches the same run's email. Run also performed first sends of the 5 subvolumes added in 01u triage (all 3 projects landed on all 3 targets; VirtualMachines parent received on 22tb — listed by btrbk list latest post-receive; 53.7 GiB total sent, 29m46s btrbk). title: backup.md: document delete-vs-mutate rule for send/receive snapshots
description: Handoff safety-rule suggestion (2026-07-31). Add to .claude/rules/backup.md: deleting a target snapshot is harmless while at least one common pair survives (source UUID == target Received UUID) — that is what target_preserve does daily. Mutation is the dangerous op: (a) never clear ro on a RECEIVED subvolume — permanently destroys Received UUID (only btrfs receive can set it) and leaves a fake-valid replica; (b) mutating an already-sent LOCAL parent silently desynchronizes source and target because btrfs send -p diffs against the local parent and never re-emits the change; nothing reports it. In-place purging of a large file is safe ONLY for snapshots that are neither send sources nor received (e.g. snapper's).
close_reason: Landed in 3faead7: 'Delete vs mutate — send/receive chain safety' subsection added to .claude/rules/backup.md with all four facts (common-pair survival, never clear ro on received, sent-local-parent mutation desync, snapper-only in-place purge). Review APPROVED.

title: Reconcile scripts/ path drift between templates.rs and CMakeLists.txt (DAS_SCRIPT_DIR)
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-23 during DAS-Backup-Manager-0p2 fix: indexer/src/setup/templates.rs lines 16, 282, 570 reference "${prefix}/lib/das-backup/scripts/" as the install path for production scripts, but CMakeLists.txt installs to DAS_SCRIPT_DIR=${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/lib/das-backup (no scripts/ subdir). Historical installs left both paths populated: real files at /usr/lib/das-backup/<name>.sh (canonical, where cmake installs) AND duplicates at /usr/lib/das-backup/scripts/<name>.sh (orphan).

Tonight (2026-05-23 23:19 CDT) I replaced the three orphan files (backup-run.sh, backup-verify.sh, boot-archive-cleanup.sh) under /usr/lib/das-backup/scripts/ with symlinks to ../<name>.sh as a short-term single-canonical-source patch. The deeper cleanup is to align the Rust code with cmake's install layout (or vice versa) so future re-installs do not regress.

Suggested approach: pick one canonical layout (cmake's flat /usr/lib/das-backup/ is cleaner) and update the templates.rs comments + test assertions + any production paths to match. Verify by reinstalling from clean state and checking only one copy lands on disk.

Cross-refs: DAS-Backup-Manager-0p2 (the trigger), .claude/rules/development-tools.md Single Canonical Source rule.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-08-02 in 08a6a07. GeneratedFiles::generate() now installs the three real embedded scripts flat at {prefix}/lib/das-backup/ (cmake's canonical layout); render_backup_run() wrapper + test deleted; regression-guard test asserts das-backup/scripts/ never reappears. PROOF: cargo test 278/0 (exactly 279 minus deleted wrapper test), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean; live migration verified — manifest 12->11 entries all flat, orphaned /usr/lib/das-backup/scripts/ symlink dir removed after zero-reference grep across /etc/das-backup + systemd units + cron + repo; md5sum identity installed-vs-repo for all three scripts; SECOND setup --upgrade idempotent (no scripts/ regeneration, checksums unchanged — the two-writer accident is gone); setup --check all 11 present; systemctl cat ExecStart flat. Adversarially reviewed: 2 doc fixes folded into commit (ARCHITECTURE.md dead render_backup_run row, CHANGELOG CMakeLists pointer); spawned trackers: e23 (upgrade no-prune), 2lj (stale-binary include_str hazard), vks (INSTALL.md stale filename — will close in this session's docs sweep).

title: IndexBackupHistory signature mismatch: helper expects (sx), Qt passes positional s,x
description:
During the 2026-05-12 fix for DAS-Backup-Manager-29j, probing each of the six cascade methods on the now-running helper revealed that IndexBackupHistory's expected signature is reported by zbus as '(sx)' — a single struct argument of (string, int64) — not two positional args 's,x'.

The Qt call at gui/src/dbusclient.cpp:361 invokes the method as:
    m_interface->call(QStringLiteral("IndexBackupHistory"), dbPath, limit);

QDBusInterface::call() with positional args usually serializes to D-Bus signature 'sx' (two scalars), not '(sx)' (one struct). If this mismatch is real, the Backup History pane will throw a method-level error post-fix (the activation cascade hid this until now).

UNCONFIRMED: only running the GUI against the now-functional helper will reveal whether QDBusInterface auto-wraps positional args into a struct or whether the mismatch is genuine. If genuine, fix at either side:
  - Helper side: change the Rust signature to accept (s, x) as two positional args (likely a one-line zbus annotation change)
  - GUI side: pass the args wrapped in a QVariant/QDBusArgument that serializes to (sx)

Recommended: helper-side fix, so signature matches the GUI's natural calling convention.
close_reason: Not reproducible. User verified GUI works end-to-end 2026-05-12 — Backup History pane populates correctly, which means IndexBackupHistory succeeded. Qt's QDBusInterface::call() apparently auto-wraps positional (s, x) args into the (sx) struct signature zbus expects. zbus reporting '(sx)' on no-arg probe was misleading; not an actual signature mismatch.
